findings.title: NW corner: north and west walls stop short, leaving an open notch to the sky; wall ends also overhang the rounded slab corner
findings.evidence: iso_se.png top-left (x 630-660, y 0-20): sky shows between the end of the west wall and the start of the north wall (crops/nw_corner.png). iso_nw.png bottom-right (x 940-975, y 840-970): the same gap, with the first oak slat visible through it. audit_nwcorner_before.png: pale sky sliver at x 550-580. Fix verified in audit_nwcorner_after.png: a curved corner wall closes the gap and the bookcase stays clear of it. The analyzer does not flag this because it checks AABB support, not gaps.
findings.location: public/js/theme-grounds.js:114 (north wall box 23.2 wide, x -11.6..11.6), :116 (west wall box 15.2 deep, z -7.6..7.6), :100-101 (corner cylinders r=1.5 at (+-10.8, +-6.8)), :115 (slat loop starting at x=-11); public/js/furniture.js:115 (westmost bookcase x=-10.4)
findings.rootCause: Both walls are plain rectangles shortened by 0.4 at each end (FLOOR_W-0.8 / FLOOR_D-0.8) to dodge the rounded slab corner, but nothing fills that corner. The square x[-12.21,-11.6] x z[-8.21,-7.6] is empty. The outer wall corners, e.g. (-11.6,-8.21) and (-12.21,-7.6), sit 1.62 from the fillet centre while the 16-gon slab edge reaches only 1.47, so about 0.15 of each wall end hangs over the void.
findings.fix: Add a curved corner wall that follows the fillet: 4 chord boxes (M.wall, 2.7 tall, 0.22 thick) around centre (-10.8,-6.8), centreline radius 1.3. For i=0..3: phi=(i+0.5)*PI/8, length=2*1.3*sin(PI/16)+0.06=0.567, position (-10.8-1.275*sin(phi), 0, -6.8-1.275*cos(phi)), then set the returned mesh's rotation.y=phi. Trim the north wall to box(g, M.wall, 22.4, 2.7, 0.22, 0.4, 0, -8.1) (x -10.8..11.6) and the west wall to box(g, M.wall, 0.22, 2.7, 14.4, -12.1, 0, 0.4) (z -6.8..7.6). Move the westmost bookcase in furniture.js:115 from x -10.4 to -10.15 (list [-10.15, -8, -5.6]); otherwise its back corner (-11.4,-7.9), 1.25 from the fillet centre, sits inside the arc wall band (1.165..1.385). Start the slat loop at x=-9.9, because the x=-11 slat would end up embedded in the arc. Deliberately left: the north wall's NE end and the west wall's S end also overhang their fillets by about 0.15, but those are open cutaway sides with no wall to curve into; optionally end the north wall at x=11.45. Optional hygiene: start the slats at y 0.02 instead of 0.1; they currently float 0.1 above the slab top, mostly hidden behind furniture.
findings.contractRisk: none. The archive-shelves obstacle (x -11.4..-4.6) still covers the shifted bookcase, and slot [-10.4,-6.3,N] still faces it. buildOfficeGround has its own walls and is unaffected.
findings.verifyNote: The defect is real at the default camera. crops/nw_corner.png and room_archive.png (x 680-750, y 0-270) show sky between the wall ends, and low_w.png (x 275-285, y 600-715) shows the x=-11 oak slat through the gap. The code agrees: the north wall (theme-grounds.js:114) ends at x -11.6 and the west wall (:116) ends at z -7.6, so the 0.61 x 0.61 corner square is empty. I checked the fix math. A chord box with rotation.y=phi maps local +x to (cos phi, -sin phi), which is tangent to the radius (-sin phi, -cos phi). The box is axis-aligned before R, so T*R*S gives no shear. The chord overlap holds at the outer face (11.57 deg against 11.25 deg). The outer corners sit at r 1.414, inside the 1.47 slab apothem. The bookcase at -10.15 has its corner at r 1.154, under the inner apothem of 1.165 (1 cm clear). audit_nwcorner_after.png renders cleanly.
findings.fixCorrection: Fix as proposed, with two corrections to contractRisk. (a) furniture.js:115 is shared with office (buildArchive), so office's west bookcase also shifts 0.25. That is harmless but not 'none'. (b) The arc's inner face, about (-11.62,-7.62) at 45 deg, lies in the NW pocket that no obstacle covers (x -11.88..-11.4, z -7.85..-6.75). The pocket is 0.48 wide against an agent diameter of 0.48, so agents cannot reach it. Rate the risk low, not none.

findings.title: Research satellite dish renders as a grey crescent or scythe on a pole
findings.evidence: Visible as a crescent blade in iso_se.png (x 320-355, y 500-600), room_research.png (x 930-1020, y 545-610), room_lounge_w.png (x 520-610, y 845-910), exterior_s.png and room_meeting.png. In top.png it is only a grey teardrop. audit_globe_after.png has the dish switched to DoubleSide, and it then reads as a dome or dish. Rated P0 under the scale's 'wrong shape visible at the default iso_se camera' clause; it is small, about 40 px.
findings.location: public/js/furniture.js:190-192 (open SphereGeometry cap, radius 0.42, thetaLength PI/2.6, shared single-sided M.metal, rotation (-0.9,0.6,0)); mast :188-189; tip :193-194
findings.rootCause: The open spherical cap is a single surface. MeshStandardMaterial defaults to FrontSide, so from the default camera, which looks into the concave side, the inner faces are culled and only a sliver of the outer rim is drawn.
findings.fix: In mats() add metalDS: themed('--metal', { roughness: 0.45, metalness: 0.35, side: THREE.DoubleSide }) so the material stays themed, and use it for the dish. To make it read clearly as a dish, also add a feed arm (CylinderGeometry(0.015, 0.015, 0.38, 6)) along the dish axis, add a 0.07 box at its end as the receiver, and move the blinking lamp tip onto that box.
findings.contractRisk: none. Office uses the same buildResearch, so it gets the same fix.
findings.verifyNote: The crescent is real (iso_se.png x 320-355, room_research.png, audit_globe_before.png) and the back-face-culling root cause is correct. The geometry shows a second problem the audit missed. The cap's centre of curvature (-4.7,1.85,7.3) sits on the mast top, so the shell floats 0.42 from the mast. With rotation (-0.9,0.6,0) the cap axis is (0,0.62,-0.78), so the bowl opens down and south (geometry.json AABB y 1.515..2.539). The lamp tip (box bottom 1.9) also floats 0.1 above the mast top (1.8). Applying DoubleSide alone gives a lampshade or street lamp hanging off the pole, not a dish: $AUDIT_OUT/captures/studio/audit_verify_dish_ds_only.png. A re-oriented bowl reads as a satellite dish at the default camera: $AUDIT_OUT/captures/studio/audit_verify_dish_reorient.png (patch: scratchpad/verify_studio/dish_reorient.js). I verified this at the default camera only; my SW render did not frame the dish.
findings.fixCorrection: In mats() add metalDS = themed('--metal', {roughness:0.45, metalness:0.35, side:THREE.DoubleSide}). In buildResearch (furniture.js:190-194), keep the mast and set: const d = new THREE.Vector3(0.4,0.75,0.5).normalize(); const V = new THREE.Vector3(-4.7,1.84,7.3) (bowl vertex on the mast top). Create the dish with metalDS, call dish.quaternion.setFromUnitVectors(new THREE.Vector3(0,1,0), d.clone().negate()) instead of rotation.set(-0.9,0.6,0), and set dish.position = V + 0.42*d. Add a feed strut CylinderGeometry(0.015,0.015,0.21,6), oriented with setFromUnitVectors(+Y, d) and placed at V + 0.105*d. Move the blinking tip to V + 0.21*d (the focus). The dish then spans x up to about -4.23 (0.17 clear of the x=-4 glass) and z up to about 7.78. The change touches props only, so contract risk is none; office gets the same change.

findings.title: Opening elevator doors slide off the frame and float in front of the bare wall, with no opening behind them
findings.evidence: iso_se.png (x 280-410, y 160-330): two black door slabs sit outside the grey frame while an agent arrives (crops/elevator_iso.png). audit_elevator_open_before.png: doors hang over the bare wall, and the solid grey frame face shows between them, so there is no opening. Fix verified in audit_elevator_open_after.png: a wider frame keeps both open doors inside it and a light cab panel shows between them. Analyzer walkThrough also hits the elevator frame and doors (expected, agents spawn there).
findings.location: public/js/theme-grounds.js:398-403 (frame 0.35 x 2.5 x 2.2 gives z +-1.1; doors 0.85 wide at z +-0.46, x+0.18); public/js/floor.js:197-199 (o = 0.46 + doorOpen*0.78, so fully open doors centre at z +-1.24 and span 0.815..1.665)
findings.rootCause: The 0.78 travel pushes 0.565 m of each 0.85 m door past the frame edge at 1.1. The doors sit at x -11.68..-11.60 while the bare wall face is at x -11.99, so the off-frame part floats 0.31 m in front of the wall with no track. The frame is a solid box, so the gap between open doors shows grey metal instead of a cab.
findings.fix: Add parameters: buildElevatorDoors(g, frameMat, doorMat, x, z, { depth = 2.2, cabMat = null } = {}). Studio (and office) pass depth 3.4 (z +-1.7, which covers 1.665) and a cab material, e.g. MeshStandardMaterial({color: 0xd8dde3, emissive: 0x3a4250, roughness: 0.5}). In the helper: frame box(frameMat, 0.35, 2.5, depth, x, 0, z); if cabMat, add box(cabMat, 0.02, 2.1, 1.7, x+0.185, 0, z, false); place the doors at x+0.24 instead of x+0.18 so they sit in front of the cab panel. Optionally add the floor-indicator lamp box(M.lamp, 0.06, 0.12, 0.5, x+0.2, 2.32, z), as already done in buildLounge (furniture.js:265). Leave the floor.js travel unchanged so the other themes behave as before. Palace and hanok gates use the same 0.78 travel against posts at +-1.25/+-1.2; flag that to those audits.
findings.contractRisk: Shared helper: the defaults keep office, starship, dogs and cats unchanged. Do not widen dogs/cats yet, since their frames already float outside the footprint (CONFIRMED #3). The wider frame protrudes to x -11.645 over |z| 1.1..1.7, which the wall-west-n/s boxes (x up to -11.88) do not cover. Agents spawn at x -11.2 (body reaches -11.51), so nothing collides. Optional studio/office-only boxes 'elevator-jamb-n' {x0:-11.88, x1:-11.6, z0:-1.75, z1:-0.9} and a mirrored 'elevator-jamb-s' pass the copied contract test, and safeSpawnPos(-11.2,0) stays at (-11.2,0). Do not change the shared wall-west boxes.
findings.verifyNote: The defect is real. The math checks out: open o = 0.46+0.78 = 1.24, so each door spans |z| 0.815..1.665 against a frame edge at 1.1. The doors sit at x -11.68..-11.60 and the wall face is at -11.99. crops/elevator_iso.png and audit_elevator_open_before.png show both doors hanging past the frame, and audit_elevator_open_after.png shows the fix working. The doors open only on arrivals and departures (elevT 1.4 s), so P1 is correct.
findings.fixCorrection: As written, the fix leaks through the shared helper: moving the doors to x+0.24 unconditionally also moves the starship, dogs and cats doors. Keep the doors at x+0.18. The cab, box(cabMat, 0.02, 2.1, 1.7, x+0.185, 0, z, false) at x -11.645..-11.625, sits strictly inside the door slab's x range (-11.68..-11.60) with no coplanar faces. Closed doors hide it and open doors reveal it, so the doors do not need to move. Alternatively, apply the 0.24 offset only when cabMat is set. Also resolve the inconsistency in the audit: if office passes depth 3.4, office changes, so only starship, dogs and cats keep the defaults. Leave floor.js travel unchanged.

findings.title: Research globe (1.6 m sphere) is boxed only at the pedestal; agents walking around it put their heads inside the globe
findings.evidence: audit_globe_before.png: an agent placed at the legal collision limit (x -8.72, z 4.75, i.e. box edge -8.5 minus walking radius 0.2) is swallowed, with only a hand and a leg visible under the sphere. room_research.png and room_lounge_w.png also show agents pressed into the globe. Fix A verified in audit_globe_propfix.png: same agent position, head now under the raised, smaller globe. Fix B: audit_globe_after.png shows an agent at the new box edge (x -9.12) clear of the globe. This verifies clearance at that boundary only; the box change itself is verified by the copied contract test (patches/studio/jscopy/check.test.mjs: all slots and door-to-slot routes in all 7 themes, plus the findSafePath(-8,2.9,-8,6.6) detour, pass). The analyzer pedestal/globe 'intersect' hit is fine (the real gap is 0.03).
findings.location: public/js/furniture.js:169-183 (pedestal CylinderGeometry(0.2,0.3,0.95) at y 0.475; ball IcosahedronGeometry(0.8,2) plus wire 0.84, group at y 1.78); public/js/theme-layouts.js:191-193 (research-globe box x -8.5..-7.5, z 4.5..5.5)
findings.rootCause: obstaclesOf boxes only +-0.5 around the pedestal, while the sphere spans +-0.8 at y 0.98..2.58. The agent head is centred at y 1.44 with radius 0.31 (agent-mesh.js:9,333). At head height the sphere section radius is 0.72, so the head needs at least 1.06 horizontal distance from the globe axis (3D: 0.8+0.31 with dy 0.34). Collision allows 0.7 when walking (0.74 at a slot radius of 0.24), about 0.36 of overlap.
findings.fix: Fix A (preferred, layouts unchanged): raise and shrink the globe. Pedestal CylinderGeometry(0.1, 0.26, 1.6, 12) at y 0.8; globe.position.y 2.2; ball IcosahedronGeometry(0.55, 2); wire IcosahedronGeometry(0.58, 1). At 0.7 horizontal, the distance between head and globe centres is sqrt(0.7^2+0.76^2)=1.03, more than 0.55+0.31=0.86. The globe bottom (1.65) is above any part of an agent at that distance. Fix B (if the large globe is kept): add a studio/office-only research-globe box {x0:-8.9, x1:-7.1, z0:4.1, z1:5.9}, giving 1.1 walking and 1.14 slot clearance, both at least 1.06. Hanok and the other themes keep their own boxes. With B, the door-to-[-8,6.6] route becomes (-6.8,4.1) -> (-6.8,6.1) -> (-8,6.6).
findings.contractRisk: A: none. B: changes obstaclesOf for studio and office only. The copied browser-names obstacle test loop passes, including slot [-6.6,5,W] (needs x >= -6.86) and [-8,6.6,N] (needs z >= 6.14).
findings.verifyNote: The audit's numbers match the code: head SphereGeometry(0.31) at y 1.44 (agent-mesh.js:9,333), globe radius 0.8 centred at y 1.78 (furniture.js:174-175), and the obstacle box at +-0.5 (theme-layouts.js:193). findSafePath runs on a 0.4 grid with r 0.2, so the detour to slot [-8,6.6] passes about 0.7-0.8 from the axis. At 0.8 horizontal the 3D distance is 0.87, below the 1.11 needed. audit_globe_before.png and room_lounge_w.png (purple agent pressed into the globe) agree. Fix A: at 0.7 horizontal the distance is sqrt(0.49+0.578) = 1.03, above 0.86, so the head clears; the head is clear from 0.40 horizontal outward. Fix B: I re-ran patches/studio/jscopy/check.test.mjs (2/2 pass) and checked the slot margins ([-6.6,5] needs x >= -6.86; [-8,6.6] needs z >= 6.14).

findings.title: Translucent glass partitions cast fully opaque shadows, so the corridor reads as lined with solid low walls
findings.evidence: iso_se.png and center.png: hard grey bands on the corridor and room floors beside every 0.34-opacity glass panel. audit_glass_shadow_before.png vs audit_glass_shadow_after.png: with castShadow off on the glass, the bands disappear, only the thin oak cap shadow remains, and the panels read as glass.
findings.location: public/js/theme-grounds.js:147 and :152 (corridor partition panels), :156-157 (x=+-4 room dividers). All are box() calls that cast shadows by default; studio passes tm.glassWall at :117.
findings.rootCause: box() casts shadows regardless of material transparency, and the three.js shadow map ignores opacity.
findings.fix: In buildStandardPartitions add const sh = !wallMat.transparent; and pass sh as the 9th argument of the four wall boxes (lines 147, 152, 156, 157). Keep the cap boxes (148, 153) casting so the rail still grounds the partition.
findings.contractRisk: none. Office passes opaque M.part, so its shadows are unchanged.
findings.verifyNote: The shadow bands are real and three.js ignores opacity in the shadow map, but the improvement is subtle (audit_glass_shadow_before/after.png). My render shows a side effect the audit missed. The x=+-4 room dividers (theme-grounds.js:156-157) have no cap rail, so their shadow band is their only visual cue. With castShadow off they become a faint pale line while the div-* obstacle boxes still block agents: compare $AUDIT_OUT/captures/studio/audit_verify_divider_before.png with audit_verify_divider_noshadow.png. The guard itself is correct. Office uses an opaque M.part, and Floor.setShadows keeps the castShadow=false recorded in userData.
findings.fixCorrection: Apply the sh = !wallMat.transparent guard as proposed, and in the same change add the divider caps from studio-m01, box(g, capMat, 0.16, 0.06, 5.92, x, 0.9, +-5.04). Without the caps the studio dividers become near-invisible walls.

findings.title: Balcony pods: oak ellipse top is coplanar with the slab top, causing a tan wedge or z-fight where the pod meets the slab rim
findings.evidence: crops/iso_se_bay_w.png and crops/iso_se_bay_e.png (default camera): tan notch at the west end of each pod where the oak rim lies on the slab rim strip. crops/top_sw.png: striped z-fight at both junctions in top.png. audit_bayrim_before.png (x 285-360, y 670-720) vs audit_bayrim_after.png: the wedge is gone and the slab strip is uniform. The faint dotted lines inside the rugs in top.png are tessellation seams that look the same before and after, so they are not part of this defect.
findings.location: public/js/theme-grounds.js:103-106 (oak cylinder 2.6 x 1.6, h 0.45 from y -0.45, top at 0; floor disc 2.3 x 1.35, h 0.03 from y 0)
findings.rootCause: The oak ellipse (z 6.0..9.2) has its top at y=0, the same height as both slab boxes over z 6.0..8.3. Where the 0.02 floor box does not cover it (rim strip z 7.8..8.3), the two coplanar surfaces fight.
findings.fix: Use cyl(g, tm.studioOak, 2.6, 1.6, 0.45, x, -0.465, 7.6) (top at -0.015, below the slab) and cyl(g, M.floor, 2.3, 1.35, 0.045, x, -0.015, 7.6) (top stays at 0.03 with no gap over the oak). Optionally set castShadow=false on both, since they are flat surfaces under everything else.
findings.contractRisk: none
findings.verifyNote: The defect is real. The oak ellipse top (theme-grounds.js:104, y -0.45 + 0.45 = 0) is coplanar with the slab top over the rim strip at z 7.8..8.3, where the floor box (top 0.02, z <= 7.8) does not cover it. crops/top_sw.png shows z-fight stripes, iso_se_bay_w.png shows the tan wedge, and my SW render audit_verify_dish_reorient_sw.png also shows the wedge at the east junction. The fix numbers are right: oak top -0.015, disc -0.015..0.03, still above the 0.02 floor and below the 0.04 rug. audit_bayrim_after.png is clean. I re-rated it from P2 to P1 because the severity scale lists z-fighting under P1. The area is small.

findings.title: Solid props with no collision box (dev tower, desk-room plant); sofa arms stick out past the sofa box
findings.evidence: Analyzer walkThrough: Box #20262e at furniture.js:148 (dev tower, x -3.6..-3.1, z -2.975..-2.525, h 0.95) and Cylinder #b8875a from plant() called at furniture.js:242 (desk plant pot, x 4.73..5.27, z 7.11..7.69). geometry.json: sofa arms (furniture.js:248-249) span x 9.02..11.18, while the lounge-sofa box is x 9.1..11.1.
findings.location: public/js/furniture.js:148, :242, :248-249; public/js/theme-layouts.js:205-209 (studio/office extras), :203 (lounge-sofa in the shared base list)
findings.rootCause: The studio/office extras block lists archive-cabinet and lounge-water but not these props. The lounge-sofa box lives in the base list shared by every theme, so it cannot be widened just for studio.
findings.fix: Add to the studio/office block: {x0:-3.65, x1:-3.05, z0:-3.0, z1:-2.5, tag:'dev-tower'} and {x0:4.7, x1:5.3, z0:7.1, z1:7.7, tag:'desk-plant'}; both pass the copied contract test. findings.verifyNote: geometry.json and the analyzer confirm the dev tower (-3.6..-3.1, -2.975..-2.525), the desk pot (4.71..5.29, 7.11..7.69) and the sofa arms (9.02..11.18) all sit outside the boxes in theme-layouts.js:203-209. findings.title: Archive cabinet and dev tower are blank cubes that read as nothing; the dev tower's top sits at rail height and looks sliced by the rail
findings.evidence: room_archive.png (grey cube at x 255-395, y 335-515; black cube at x 990-1080, y 760-900), iso_se.png (x 450-510, y 175-240 and x 758-795, y 368-425), center.png (x 715-810, y 115-275). findings.location: public/js/furniture.js:138 (box M.metal 0.8 x 1.2 x 0.7 at (-11.3, -3.1)), :148 (box M.dark 0.5 x 0.95 x 0.45 at (-3.35, -2.75))
findings.rootCause: Single untextured boxes with no detail. The dev box height (0.95) roughly matches the partition cap (0.9-0.96), so from the default camera the rail lines up with its top edge.
findings.fix: Archive cabinet: make it a filing cabinet. Add 2 drawer seams box(M.dark, 0.012, 0.015, 0.62, -10.895, y, -3.1, false) at y 0.4 and 0.8 on the +x face, 3 handles box(M.wood, 0.03, 0.04, 0.22, -10.885, y, -3.1, false) at y 0.2, 0.6 and 1.0, and an archive box on top: box(M.wood, 0.45, 0.22, 0.36, -11.3, 1.2, -3.1). The footprint stays the same, so the studio-07 'dev-tower' box still applies.
findings.contractRisk: none (footprints unchanged)
findings.verifyNote: The readability part holds: the archive cabinet and dev tower are plain boxes (room_archive.png, center.png). The 'sliced by the rail' root cause and the 0.6 m fix are wrong. At the default camera (dir 1,0.92,1) the 0.9-0.96 cap visually crosses anything closer than about 1.05 m behind it, whatever its height. The covered height is about 0.96 - 0.92*depth behind the cap's back edge. The tower front sits only 0.6 behind the cap, so lowering it cannot help. My renders confirm the rail still crosses the tower at 0.6 m and at 0.4 m: $AUDIT_OUT/captures/studio/audit_verify_devtower_0.6.png and audit_verify_devtower_0.4.png.
findings.fixCorrection: Archive cabinet: keep the proposed drawer seams, handles and top box. Dev tower: do not lower it; move it deeper into the room. Option 1: box(g, M.dark, 0.5, 0.95, 0.45, -3.35, 0, -3.4) (front face z -3.175, 1.1 behind the cap, so the rail clears), with the studio-07 box moved to {x0:-3.65, x1:-3.05, z0:-3.65, z1:-3.15}. The 0.23 gap to div-top-w is too narrow for an agent (needs 0.48), so it cannot trap one, and it is far from slot [-1.3,-3.1] and the door routes. Option 2: a 0.24 x 0.5 x 0.45 PC tower under the west dev desk at (-3.25, 0, -6.95). It clears the legs at x -3.55..-3.49, sits below the 0.72 underside and inside the 'dev-desks' box, so it needs no new obstacle. Keep the LED and vent dressing in both options.

findings.title: Rail-height props pressed against the glass partitions look like they clip through them (west lounge plant, dev plant, sofa back)
findings.evidence: entrance.png (x 615-710, y 530-700) and room_lounge_w.png (x 515-610, y 445-560): the oak rail runs through the foliage of the plant by the elevator. The leaf AABB z-max of 1.928 overlaps the cap's z-min of 1.92 at y 0.9-0.96. room_dev.png (x 835-935, y 655-800): the dev plant, foliage top 1.24, sits 0.37 behind the rail, which visually cuts through it. room_lounge_e.png (x 660-950, y 550-750) and room_server.png: the sofa back (top 0.97) is 0.04 in front of the glass and level with the cap (0.96), so it reads as stuffed into the partition. Apart from the 0.008 leaf/cap graze, nothing actually intersects; the problem is how close and level these props are.
findings.rootCause: The props are placed flush against the 0.9 m glass partitions and are as tall as or taller than the rail, so from the south-east camera the rail draws across them.
findings.fix: Change to plant(g, -10.4, 1.25, 0.9), giving foliage z-max 1.63, 0.29 clear of the cap. Change the dev plant to plant(g, 3.3, -3.05, 0.75), giving foliage top 1.04 and 0.6 m behind the rail. Lower the sofa back to box(g, M.sofa, 2.0, 0.33, 0.16, 10.1, 0.42, 1.78) (top 0.75, below the 0.9 cap) and keep the arms at 0.62.
findings.contractRisk: none. Lounge slots at z -1.3 and x <= 10.4, and elevator spawn (-11.2, 0), stay clear. The moved plant at z 1.25 (pot r 0.2) is 1.05 from the spawn line.
findings.verifyNote: No clipping exists. geometry.json gives the elevator-side plant's leaf an AABB z-max of 1.872, not the audit's 1.928, so it sits 0.048 clear of the cap at z-min 1.92. The sofa back and dev plant do not touch the glass either. What the screenshots show is ordinary occlusion by a foreground rail. By the projection rule in studio-08, the rail crosses anything within about 1.05 m behind it from the default camera. Two of the three proposed moves do not fix that. The lounge plant at z 1.25 would still be crossed at the pot by the z=+2 rail, since anything in the corridor clears that rail only when its front is at z < 0.88, which is inside the walking lanes. A sofa back topping out at 0.75 puts its top edge inside the rail band (about 0.57-0.92 at z 1.72-1.88), which looks worse than the current back, which shows above the rail. The dev plant at z -3.05 still grazes the pot (band top at about 0.22).
findings.fixCorrection: Recategorise from clipping to readability, P2. Dev plant: plant(g, 3.3, -3.35, 0.75); the pot front is 1.1 behind the cap, so the rail clears it. West lounge plant: move it to the north side of the corridor, plant(g, -10.4, -1.3, 0.9), so the z=-2 rail is behind it. Lounge slots are at x >= 0.8, lounge overflow candX >= -6.2, and the spawn point (-11.2,0) is 1.5 away, so no contract change. Sofa: leave it as is. A back low enough to sit wholly under the rail band (top <= 0.56) no longer reads as a sofa back, and the lounge-sofa box is shared by every theme.

merged.notes:
The repo was not modified. All evidence filenames are relative to $AUDIT_OUT/captures/studio/ (crops in crops/; my renders are named audit_*).

Tooling caveats:
- The shared shot.py patch mode fails on this server. It runs the patch through eval, which the page's Content Security Policy blocks. I used a copy with bypass_csp=True: $AUDIT_OUT/patches/studio/shot2.py. The patches are in the same folder: corner_fix.js, elevator_fix.js, bay_fix.js, glass_noshadow.js, globe_before/after/prop_fix.js, closed.js and noop.js.
- In #demo mode the camera framing drifts between runs, so before/after pairs are not always pixel-aligned. Treat them as qualitative evidence.
- audit_entrance_open*.png in the studio captures folder were written by another agent, not me.

Contract verification: copies of placement.js, rooms.js, theme-layouts.js and legend-data.js are in $AUDIT_OUT/patches/studio/jscopy/. There, the research-globe box was enlarged for studio/office and dev-tower, desk-plant and elevator-jamb-n/s boxes were added. check.test.mjs replicates the obstacle test in test/browser-names.test.mjs: every slot is clear at r 0.24, door-to-slot routes are clear at r 0.16, and the research-globe detour holds. It also checks that safeSpawnPos(-11.2, 0) is unchanged. It passes for all 7 themes. Re-run the real suite (node --test test/*.test.mjs) after applying.

Analyzer leads I judged fine:
- The 22 intersects between the north wall and the oak slats: the slats are deliberately embedded 0.03 into the wall face.
- The 2 intersects between the elevator frame and its doors: the doors are mounted on the frame.
- The pedestal/globe AABB overlap: the real gap is 0.03.
- The sofa base/arm overlaps: same prop.
- The Review Booth beacon floatingGlow: an intentional hologram, though the readability idea is under improvements.
- The wall-south and wall-east invisibleObstacle hits: studio is a cutaway diorama, and those boxes are what keep agents on the slab. Agents also cannot reach the pods.
- The meeting-board invisibleObstacle (coverage 0.24): the 4.4 m board on legs really does block, so the box is correct.
- The elevator walkThrough: agents spawn there by design.
- Plants near the x=+-4 dividers (meeting and desk room) do not intersect the glass; the glass legitimately renders in front of them.
- The Review Booth monitors face the remote-reviewer beacon (east), away from agent slot [8.3,5,E]. That is consistent with the 'present to reviewer' metaphor, so I did not report it.

Shared-helper and cross-theme notes for the planner:
- buildElevatorDoors (studio-03) is used by office, starship, dogs and cats. Keep the default parameter so the others are unchanged until their audits.
- floor.js door travel 0.78 also pushes the palace and hanok gate doors (0.85 wide at +-0.46) into their posts at +-1.25 and +-1.2.
- buildStandardPartitions (studio-05) is used by office with an opaque material; the transparency guard keeps office's shadows.
- Office uses every studio furniture builder, so studio-02, -04, -07, -08 and -09 and most improvements also land in office. Office's buildOfficeGround does not share studio-01, -05 or -06.

Suggested order: studio-01 (P0, about 10 lines), studio-02 (P0, one material), studio-03 (helper parameter), studio-04 option A (furniture only), then the P2s.

findings.title: Open elevator reads as two loose grey pillars: doors slide past the 2.2 m frame and the gap shows only a white wall
findings.evidence: Default camera, stock capture $AUDIT_OUT/captures/office/iso_se.png, top left around (280-410, 175-330): two grey slabs stand far apart in front of the west wall, with a white block above and no opening. Same in .../captures/office/audit_iso_se_open.png and close up in .../captures/office/audit_elev_open.png (doors forced open). The fix was tested in-page: .../captures/office/audit_elev_fix.png and .../captures/office/audit_elev_fix_wide.png show a dark cab, both doors on the frame and a lamp. Closed state (entrance.png) looks fine. Analyzer: walkThrough plus intersect hits on the frame and doors are a benign door/frame overlap.
findings.location: theme-grounds.js:398-403 (buildElevatorDoors), called from theme-grounds.js:138 (office) and :118 (studio); door travel in floor.js:195-199
findings.rootCause: floor.update moves each door centre to z = ±(0.46 + 0.78·doorOpen) = ±1.24. With a 0.85 door depth the outer edge reaches ±1.665, but the frame is only ±1.1, so each door hangs 0.565 past the frame in front of the bare wall. Nothing is placed behind the doors, so the opening shows the frame's front face. In office that face is M.wall, the same colour as the wall, so there is no visible cab or opening. This happens on every agent arrival (openElevator sets elevT = 1.4 s).
findings.fix: Change the helper to buildElevatorDoors(g, frameMat, doorMat, x, z, frameW = 2.2) and make three edits. (1) Frame: box(g, frameMat, 0.35, 2.5, frameW, x, 0, z). (2) Add a cab panel that the closed doors hide: box(g, mats().dark, 0.02, 2.1, 1.78, x + 0.19, 0, z, false). It spans x+0.18..x+0.20, which is 0.005 in front of the frame face (x+0.175) and 0.02 behind the door fronts (x+0.22). When closed, the 0.07 gap between the doors shows a dark seam, which is a correct door-seam look. (3) Optional floor indicator: box(g, mats().lamp, 0.04, 0.1, 0.5, x + 0.2, 2.24, z, false). For office (theme-grounds.js:138) and studio (:118), pass frameW = 3.6 so the open doors (edge 1.665) stay on the frame. Leave door size and floor.js travel unchanged.
findings.contractRisk: The theme-layouts contract does not change: the elevator x/z, the lounge door and the wall-west-n/s obstacles stay as they are. With frameW = 3.6, the frame between |z| = 1.1 and 1.8 sits 0.235 east of the wall-west obstacles. This is cosmetic: agents spawn at (-11.2, 0) and walk lanes with |z| ≤ 0.7, and the closest partitions start at |z| = 1.94. The cab panel is safe for all seven themes because closed doors always cover it. Widen the frame only in themes with nothing within |z| ≤ 1.8 on the west wall; office and studio were checked, palace/hanok gates and the dogs/cats doors at x=-11.42 need their own check.
findings.verifyNote: The defect is real. iso_se.png (top left) and audit_elev_open.png show the open doors standing apart on bare wall-coloured surface. The math checks out: door centre ±(0.46+0.78) = ±1.24 and the 0.85 doors reach ±1.665, against a ±1.1 frame. It is transient, though. openElevator() is only called from agent.js:64 on spawn (elevT 1.4 s), so the broken look lasts about 2 s per arrival, and the closed state (entrance.png) is fine. Per the scale that is 'during agent movement' = P1, not P0. The fix renders well (audit_elev_fix_wide.png), but it has three problems. (1) The proposed cab panel (x+0.18..x+0.20, height 2.1) lies wholly inside the closed-door volume (x+0.14..x+0.22, height 2.1), so its top face is coplanar with both door tops at y=2.1. That makes a z-fighting strip that the high iso camera sees. The tested patch did not check the closed state. (2) The notes say buildElevatorDoors serves all 7 themes, but it is called by 5: studio :118, office :138, starship :316, dogs :358 and cats :395. Palace and hanok build their own gates (theme-grounds.js ~205-212, ~258-263) with the same floor.js travel. (3) A finished cab, door and lamp design already exists as dead code in buildLounge (furniture.js:258-267, see office-m02).
findings.fixCorrection: Same plan, with the cab panel kept below the door tops: box(g, mats().dark, 0.02, 2.06, 1.76, x + 0.19, 0, z, false). Its top is hidden 4 cm inside the closed doors and its ends stay inside ±0.885. Keep frameW = 3.6 for office (:138) and studio (:118) only, keep the lamp box at (x+0.2, 2.24), and leave door size and travel unchanged. Ship it together with office-m01 so the doors also open when an agent leaves.

findings.title: Research satellite dish reads as a scythe or sickle at the default camera
findings.evidence: Stock captures iso_se.png (thin pole with a dark crescent left of the whiteboard), room_research.png, exterior_s.png and room_lounge_w.png; close up in $AUDIT_OUT/captures/office/audit_dish_before.png. Tested fix: .../audit_dish_fix_b.png (SE) and .../audit_dish_fix_b_sw.png (SW) read as a dish with a feed arm and lamp. The rejected variant .../audit_dish_fix_a.png faces the camera and reads as a ball on a stick.
findings.location: furniture.js:188-195 (mast, dish, tip)
findings.rootCause: The dish is a front-side-only SphereGeometry cap (thetaLength π/2.6) with rotation (-0.9, 0.6, 0). Its convex back faces the camera and the culled inside leaves only a crescent silhouette. The blinking tip sits at the cap centre with no feed arm, and the mast top does not meet the dish's back.
findings.fix: (1) In mats() (furniture.js:17-39) add metalDS: themed('--metal', { roughness: 0.45, metalness: 0.35, side: THREE.DoubleSide }). Do not call themed() inside buildResearch: every call pushes to THEMED, so it would leak on each rebuildTheme. (2) Move the mast to (-4.9, 0.9, 7.1); its top is mastTop = (-4.9, 1.8, 7.1). (3) Set dir = new THREE.Vector3(0.75, 0.9, -0.75).normalize(). Build the dish as new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.42, 16, 8, 0, Math.PI*2, 0, Math.PI/3.2).rotateX(-Math.PI/2), M.metalDS), position it at mastTop + 0.42·dir and call dish.lookAt(position + dir). (4) Feed arm: Mesh(CylinderGeometry(0.012, 0.012, 0.3, 6).rotateX(Math.PI/2), M.metalDS) at mastTop + 0.43·dir with the same lookAt. (5) Move the blink tip to mastTop + 0.6·dir.
findings.contractRisk: None. The mast is not in obstaclesOf, and the new dish stays inside the research room (x ≤ -4.4, z ≤ 7.6).
findings.verifyNote: audit_dish_before.png and iso_se.png show a crescent or sickle, and audit_dish_fix_b.png reads as a dish. The warning about calling themed() is right: scene.js:19-25 pushes every call into THEMED. One geometry flaw: after rotateX(-π/2), lookAt(+z→dir) puts the cap at mastTop + (0..0.07)·dir, but a 0.3 arm centred at 0.43·dir spans 0.28..0.58·dir. findings.title: Leaving agents walk up to closed elevator doors and vanish: the doors never open on departure
findings.evidence: Code path, no screenshot needed. agent.js:251 (and :141 in refreshTheme) walks a 'leave' item to ELEVATOR (-11.2, 0) facing west. onArrive 'leave' (agent.js:319-321) calls office.removeAgent (office.js:328-334), which disposes the agent immediately. Floor.openElevator() (floor.js:178) has exactly one caller, agent.js:64 on spawn, so doorOpen stays 0 during departures. Every agent that leaves disappears in front of shut doors at the default camera.
findings.location: public/js/agent.js:251, 319-321 (leave handling); public/js/floor.js:178 (openElevator); public/js/agent.js:64 (only caller)
findings.rootCause: The door animation is wired only to spawning. Nothing triggers it when an agent leaves.
findings.fix: In Agent.update (agent.js ~436-460), when this.current?.kind === 'leave' and Math.hypot(pos.x - ELEVATOR.x, pos.z - ELEVATOR.z) < 2.5, call this.floor.openElevator(). This refreshes elevT to 1.4 while the agent approaches. At WALK 3.4 m/s the 2.5 m takes about 0.7 s, and the doors reach ~90% open in about 0.4 s (easing dt*6 at floor.js:196). Also call this.floor.openElevator() in the 'leave' branch of onArrive before removeAgent, so the doors close behind the agent once it disappears. With office-01's dark cab, the agent visibly 'enters'.
findings.contractRisk: None for theme-layouts, SLOTS, obstaclesOf or corridorWaypoints. No test references openElevator or leave (grep test/). It applies to every theme, because all ground builders return a door pair that floor.update slides.
findings.verifyNote: found in completeness pass

merged.notes:
Tooling: the [patch.js] argument of scratchpad/shot.py is broken for this page. The page CSP has no 'unsafe-eval', so `eval(src)` throws EvalError. A working copy is $AUDIT_OUT/shot_office.py: it inlines the patch source into the page.evaluate function, which avoids eval. The patches used are in $AUDIT_OUT/patches/ (office_elev_open.js, office_elev_fix.js, office_dish_fix2.js, office_sofa_fix.js, office_globe_head.js). Patches that move elevator doors must set floor.elevT/doorOpen, because Floor.update rewrites door z every frame.

Test strategy: node tests cannot import three.js modules, so only the obstaclesOf changes (office-02, 04A, 05, 08, improvement 1) are unit-testable. Key every new or changed box to `key === 'studio' || key === 'office'` (the block at theme-layouts.js:205), keep obs.length ≥ 20, and rely on test/browser-names.test.mjs:353-378, which recomputes slot overlap at r = 0.24 and door→slot routes for every theme. Keep the pinned assertions true: segmentHitsObstacle(-8, 2.9, -8, 6.6, 0.2, 'studio') hits, and the meeting-table point (0.8, 5) is pushed out. Do not change SLOTS, doors or the elevator for office: no finding needs it. Verify visual fixes with shot_office.py at iso_se (1 0.92 1 0 0 1) plus one close-up.

Shared code: office and studio share every furniture.js builder and buildLoungeProps, so office-02..05, 07 and 08 fix studio too. buildElevatorDoors (office-01) is called by all 7 themes. The cab panel is safe everywhere, but frameW widening must be checked per theme. buildStandardPartitions (office-09a) is used by studio and office, and possibly others.

Analyzer hits dismissed: invisibleObstacle wall-south and wall-east are the intentional camera-side cutaway (no south or east wall); meeting-board at 0.242 coverage is a thin 0.08 board inside a 0.35 box, which is fine. floatingGlow Icosahedron at furniture.js:241 is the intentional hologram core above the beacon pedestal. Intersect hits: elevator door vs frame is a benign 0.035 overlap; sofa arms vs seat is intentional layering; globe vs pedestal is the wire AABB, with an actual gap of 0.03. walkThrough on the elevator frame and doors is benign (agents spawn at x -11.2); the dev box is covered in office-05 and the desk plant in office-08. outside (terrace, ledge) is covered in office-06. No noSupport, floating, hidden or raisedFloor issues: the office floor tops are at 0.02-0.04. A coplanar-face scan of geometry.json found no visible z-fighting beyond the 2 cm floor/corridor edge sliver (office-09).

Observation, not a finding: desk-room slot (8.3, 5, E) faces the backs of both monitors, because the screens face +x toward the hologram beacon. This matches the remote-intercom comment at furniture.js:229 and keeps the screens facing the default camera, so leave it unless the booth is redesigned.

Severity: office-01 is rated P0 because the stock default iso_se.png capture already shows the detached grey slabs, and the effect recurs on every agent arrival.

findings.title: Every palace roof renders as a sheared diagonal blade or kite: 3 north eaves and the west gate
findings.evidence: captures/palace/iso_se.png: three huge dark diagonal blades over the north rooms, and the gate roof is a vertical diamond. iso_sw.png and iso_ne.png: the roofs stand up as vertical kites. exterior_n.png, room_dev.png, room_archive.png, room_server.png: the blades cut across the rooms. entrance.png: the gate roof is a tilted plank. In iso_se.png the red dots at about (650,35) and (1555,528) are the tops of the x=+-11.6 pillars poking through the green trims, which the sheared cone does not cover. After baking the rotation into the geometry the roofs are proper hip roofs and the pillar tops are hidden: EXPERIMENT_roof_fixed_iso_se.png, $AUDIT_OUT/captures/palace/audit_fixA_iso_se.png, audit_rooffix_iso_nw.png. The analyzer intersect hits roofEave cone vs trim (theme-grounds.js:64/70) belong to this cause.
findings.location: theme-grounds.js:63-71 (roofEave), called at theme-grounds.js:188, 189, 190 (north eaves) and 209 (gate)
findings.rootCause: This is CONFIRMED #1. roofEave scales CONE4 non-uniformly (w*0.74, h, d*0.74) and then sets mesh rotation.y = PI/4. three.js composes the transform as T*R*S, so the diamond is stretched first and rotated afterwards, which shears long eaves (9.2x2.4, 8.2x1.8, 1.6x3.4) into blades.
findings.fix: Add a module-level const HIP4 = new THREE.ConeGeometry(1, 1, 4).rotateY(Math.PI / 4) and use it in roofEave instead of CONE4. Delete line 68 (roof.rotation.y = Math.PI / 4). Keep scale (w*0.74, h, d*0.74), which gives a footprint of 1.046w x 1.046d: centre eave 9.63 x 2.51 (x +-4.81, z -9.36..-6.85), side eaves 8.58 x 1.88 (x 3.71..12.29), gate 1.67 x 3.56. That is about a 2% overhang over the trim box. Pillar tops at y 2.5 then sit under the roof surface (at x=11.6 the roof is at about y 2.575), so the pillars need no change. Fix the starship OCT hull the same way (rotateY(PI/8) baked into the geometry).
findings.contractRisk: No change to slots, doors or obstacles. The fix also changes hanok roofs, which use the same helper and need the same verification, and the starship OCT hull if fixed the same way.
findings.verifyNote: iso_se.png has three diagonal dark blades over the north rooms and the gate roof is a vertical diamond. iso_sw/iso_ne/iso_nw/low_w show the same roofs as kites or blades. In verify/pillar_tops_nw.png, the x=-11.6 pillar top sticks up through the green trim (pillar top 2.5, trim top 2.46). The math checks out. ConeGeometry(1,1,4) puts its vertices on the axes, so rotateY(PI/4) turns it into an axis-aligned square of half-size 0.707, and 0.707*0.74 = 0.523 per side (1.046w). At x=11.6 (dx 3.6 of 4.29) the side-eave surface is at 2.46 + 0.72*(1-0.839) = 2.576, which is above the pillar top of 2.5. At the pillar's outer edge (x 11.83) it is 2.537, still above. The gate trim (2.5..2.66) covers the gate pillar tops (2.6). The audit's fixA render and my own render with the baked geometry (verify/v2_gate_se.png) both show proper hip roofs.
findings.fixCorrection: HIP4 must be a NEW module constant. Do not rotate CONE4 in place: CONE4 is also used with uniform scale by the cats ground (theme-grounds.js:369-371), and mutating it would rotate those discs by 45 degrees. The same helper change also reshapes the three hanok roofEave calls (theme-grounds.js:234/238/260). For example, the 24.8x1.5 north eave becomes a 25.9x1.57 low pyramid, so the hanok audit must re-verify it. Leave the starship OCT hull out of this palace change. Baking PI/8 into OCT does not keep the current shape: it gives an axis-aligned stretched octagon with x extent 10.35 at z +-3.29, which differs from today's skewed footprint. It touches the starship elevator noSupport and deck, so it needs its own starship verification.

findings.contractRisk: None. The corridor-center obstacle and ring lanes are unchanged. Any new coping must stay inside z +-1.05.
findings.verifyNote: Rim top = 0 + 0.18 and water top = 0.04 + 0.14 = 0.18, so the two top faces are coplanar. The water material is transparent (furniture.js:37, opacity 0.75). The defect is visible at the default camera. verify/pond_iso_se.png (a crop of iso_se.png) shows a jagged grey staircase biting into the north-west half of the water. center.png and audit_pond_before.png show about half the water grey, and iso_sw.png shows nearly the whole pond grey. I checked the fix geometry. Coping strips z 0.825..1.05 and x 2.55..2.8 do not overlap each other. The water's bottom face at y 0.04 is coplanar with the base-plate top, but that face is back-face culled from above. The water side faces at x +-2.55 and z +-0.825 face opposite to the coping's inner faces, so neither pair z-fights. findings.title: Agents walk through the rotating armillary sphere rings (research room)
findings.evidence: room_lounge_w.png: the blue agent at about (520,650) stands inside the golden rings. room_research.png: the purple agent's head passes through the outer ring at about (790,250). The analyzer reports no hit, because the rings are dynamic (globe.rotation.y) and wider than the collision box.
findings.location: theme-props.js:108-120 (pedestal 1.1 wide, globe at y 1.65, ring scales [0.85,0.72,0.58]) vs theme-layouts.js:191-193 (research-globe box x -8.5..-7.5, z 4.5..5.5)
findings.rootCause: The torus outer radius is about s*1.06, so the outer ring (s=0.85) sweeps a 0.9 radius disc (x -8.9..-7.1, z 4.1..5.9) at y 0.75-2.55 as it spins. The collision box is the studio globe's +-0.5. With AGENT_RADIUS 0.24 and findSafePath r=0.18, an agent body can reach about 0.44 from the globe centre.
findings.sharedHelper: theme-layouts collision boxes (research-globe box shared by all non-hanok themes)
findings.fix: Primary fix, no contract change: shrink the instrument to fit the box. Ring scales [0.85,0.72,0.58] become [0.5,0.42,0.34] (sweep about 0.53, overlap under 0.1 and only at ring-equator height). Core 0.28 becomes 0.18. Globe y 1.65 becomes 1.25 (1.20 after palace-03). Pedestal 1.1x0.75x1.1 becomes 0.8x0.55x0.8 (ring bottom 0.72 stays above the pedestal top 0.58). Alternative that keeps the hero size: add a palace-only branch in obstaclesOf, research-globe {x0:-8.95, x1:-7.05, z0:4.05, z1:5.95}.
findings.contractRisk: The primary fix changes nothing. For the alternative obstacle box I checked clearance with r=0.24: slot (-6.5,5) vs x1+r=-6.81 is clear; (-8,6.7) vs z1+r=6.19 is clear; (-10.1,3.7/6.3) vs x0-r=-9.19 is clear; research door inner (-8,2.9) vs z0-r=3.81 is clear. That leaves a 1.22-wide passage between research-desks and the globe. Tests do not pin this box.
findings.verifyNote: The defect is real. Ring 1 lies in the XY plane and spins about Y, so it sweeps a sphere of radius 0.85*1.06 = 0.90 around (-8, 1.65, 5). The 1.0x1.0 box lets an agent centre come within 0.68 of the axis (findSafePath r = 0.18), and the sweep sphere reaches y 1.06 at that distance, which is torso and head height. The route from the research door (-8, 2.9) to slot (-8, 6.7) has to skirt the box, so this happens in normal walking. room_research.png and room_lounge_w.png match this. The proposed primary fix is not sufficient. With a 0.53 sweep, the agent body edge (0.44 from the axis) still overlaps at y about 0.95..1.55. It also introduces a new defect: the outer ring bottom at 1.20 - 0.53 = 0.67 floats 0.09 above the new 0.58 pedestal top. Today the ring is embedded 0.08 and reads as seated. My render verify/v3_globe.png shows the gap and a much weaker hero prop. The audit's contract note is also wrong: test/browser-names.test.mjs:353-369 does pin palace obstacles, by checking slot clearance at r 0.24 and door-to-slot routes at r 0.16 for every theme. I re-ran that exact logic on a scratch copy (verify_palace/check.mjs, plus elevator-to-slot routes at lanes +-0.7) with the enlarged box: 0 failures.
findings.fixCorrection: Make the palace-only obstacle the primary fix and keep the hero size. At theme-layouts.js:191-193 use key === 'hanok' ? {hanok box} : key === 'palace' ? { x0: -8.95, x1: -7.05, z0: 4.05, z1: 5.95, tag: 'research-globe' } : { x0: -8.5, x1: -7.5, z0: 4.5, z1: 5.5, tag: 'research-globe' }. Agent centres then stay at least 1.13 from the axis and body edges at least 0.89, against a 0.90 sweep. If the instrument is shrunk anyway, also set globe y = pedestalTop + 0.53 - 0.03 (about 1.08 with palace-03 and a 0.55 pedestal) so the ring stays seated, and still widen the box to about +-0.75.

findings.title: Gate leaves slide through the gate pillars when open and sit on the agent spawn point when closed

findings.rootCause: The leaves are on the same x line as the pillars. Opened, their 0.85 width spans z 0.815..1.665, which overlaps the pillars at z 1.03..1.47. Closed, they occupy x -11.9..-11.8 where agents appear and leave (elevator x=-11.8). Departing agents walk into them, because the gate is never reopened on departure.

Lines 210-211 become box(g, tm.vermilion, 0.1, 1.9, 0.85, -12.12, 0.02, +-0.46), so x -12.17..-12.07: clear of the pillars (min x -12.05), still on the upper slab (-12.2) and under the fixed gate roof (x -12.69..-11.01). Opened, they park behind the pillars as seen from the default camera. Closed, an agent at x=-11.8 (body -12.04..-11.56) no longer overlaps them, and resolveObstacleCollision clamps agents to x >= -11.65. Keep return [dL, dR].
findings.contractRisk: None. The elevator, doors and slots are unchanged. The test needs buildThemeGround(...).length === 2, which this keeps.
findings.verifyNote: Both claims hold. Floor.update (floor.js:197-199) slides the leaves to z +-1.24, so an open leaf spans z 0.815..1.665 inside the pillars (z 1.03..1.47, x -12.05..-11.65). audit_entrance_open.png shows the fat pillars and audit_entrance_open_sw.png the protruding edge. The palace elevator is at x -11.8 (theme-layouts.js:52), so agents spawn and leave inside the closed leaves (x -11.9..-11.8). openElevator() is called only on spawn (agent.js:64), never on departure. findings.title: roofEave shears every hanok roof into giant diagonal blades and kites
findings.evidence: iso_se.png: the north eave becomes a dark blade spanning the whole scene, and the west gate and pavilion roofs become diamond kites. findings.location: theme-grounds.js:10 (CONE4), 63-71 (roofEave: scale.set(w*0.74,h,d*0.74) then rotation.y=PI/4). Hanok call sites: 234 (north eave), 238 (pavilion eave), 260 (gate eave)
findings.rootCause: three.js composes T*R*S. The non-uniform x/z scale is applied first and the 45 deg rotation second, so a long thin diamond is turned into a diagonal blade. CONFIRMED #1.
findings.fix: In theme-grounds.js add `const ROOF4 = new THREE.ConeGeometry(1, 1, 4).rotateY(Math.PI / 4);`. In roofEave use `new THREE.Mesh(ROOF4, mat)` and delete line 68 (`roof.rotation.y = Math.PI / 4`). Keep the 0.74 factor: after baking, the half-extent is 0.74*0.707*w = 0.52w, so a roof still covers about 1.05 x w by 1.05 x d. Leave the CONE4 constant as it is, because the cats ears (theme-grounds.js:369-371) use it through cyl() with uniform scale and would turn 45 deg. This one change also fixes the 3 palace roofEave calls (188-190, 209).
findings.contractRisk: none
findings.verifyNote: iso_se.png shows the north eave as a dark blade across the whole scene, and the gate and pavilion roofs as kites. EXPERIMENT_roof_fixed_iso_se.png shows normal roofs after the rotation is baked in. theme-grounds.js:65-68 scales by (w*0.74, h, d*0.74) and then sets rotation.y PI/4; with T*R*S that gives the shear. The math works out: after ConeGeometry(1,1,4).rotateY(PI/4) the half-extent is 0.74*0.707*w = 0.52w. CONE4 is also used by the cats ears (369-371, via cyl with uniform 4.4/4.1/2.5 scale), so adding a new constant instead of editing CONE4 is correct. roofEave is only called by palace and hanok. One small error: palace has 4 calls (188, 189, 190, 209), not 3. After the fix, the 24.8 x 1.5 north eave is a single-apex pyramid (no ridge) that drops to the trim height at both ends. merged.notes:
All screenshots named above are in $AUDIT_OUT/captures/hanok/. New in this audit: audit_detail_*, audit_gate_*, audit_zfight_*, audit_scroll_*, audit_fixexp_*, audit_fixexp_open_*.

**In-page fix experiment.** $AUDIT_OUT/hanok_audit/fixes.js and fixes_open.js apply hanok-01 to -05, -07, -08, the chimney half of -09 and the hanok-03 floor lowering. Run them with `xcut/multishot.py hanok <prefix> hanok_audit/fixes.js <views>` to produce before/after comparisons. When rendering open doors, override `floor.openElevator`: demo agents call `openElevator()`, which resets `elevT` to 1.4 and closes the doors before later views (as done in fixes_open.js).

**Test strategy.**
- Node tests can only import theme-layouts.js and rooms.js.
- Every fix here except improvement 8 is geometry-only in theme-grounds.js and theme-props.js. obstaclesOf, SLOTS, doors and ELEVATOR.x (-11.6, pinned by test/browser-names.test.mjs:187) are untouched.
- test/page-approval-office.test.mjs:338-360 needs buildThemeGround to return 2 doors and buildHanokProps to return non-empty leds plus a globe. Keep both when restructuring the forge.
- Improvement 8 adds one obstacle. Obstacle count is not pinned, but re-run the hanok route test at line 189.

**Coupling and ordering.**
- hanok-08 must land together with hanok-03: lowering the floors exposes the partition gap.
- hanok-01 is shared with palace. Add a new baked constant and do not edit CONE4, because the cats ears (cyl with CONE4, theme-grounds.js:369-371) use it.
- hanok-05 and hanok-06 have palace twins (theme-grounds.js:208-211 and scrollScreen). Fix them in the shared code paths.

**Analyzer leads judged benign.**
- wall-north/south/east/west invisibleObstacle hits sit on the slab edge.
- corridor-center coverage of 0.18 is a 0.16-high flower bed inside the box.
- Gate-post walkThrough: lane offsets are capped at +-0.7, plus agent radius 0.24, which stays inside the posts' inner face at |z| 1.0.
- All 6 'outside' hits are intentional footprint extensions (east terrace, SW pavilion plinth).
- The pine/plum and boardFrame intersect hits are intended layering.

With the octagon baked (starship-08), the north edge becomes -7.95 and the x=0 nozzle would detach too.
findings.fix: Replace the loop body with a nacelle, a bell and a glow. Nacelle: `box(g, tm.hullTrim, 1.5, 0.5, 1.1, tx, -0.5, -8.0)` (z -8.55..-7.45, top at 0, under the deck, overlapping the hull for any octagon). Bell: `new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.62, 0.38, 0.9, 12), tm.hull)` with rotation.x = -PI/2 at (tx, -0.25, -8.95), wide end north. Glow: CYL plasmaCyan at scale (0.5, 0.04, 0.5), rotation.x = PI/2, at (tx, -0.25, -9.44); keep it outside the bell cap at -9.40. At z -9.38 it z-fought (pinwheel in audit_fix_exterior_n.png); at -9.44 it is clean (audit_fix_nozzles_n.png). Nothing pokes above the room decks any more (audit_fix_iso_se.png, audit_fix_top.png).

findings.verifyNote: The nozzles reading as wheels (exterior_n.png, iso_ne.png) and as dark drums behind the dev desks (iso_se.png, room_dev.png) is a theme-identity problem, so P2 on the scale, not geometry breakage. The detachment is real only at x=-5.5. The pod edge is at z -7.80 at the nozzle centre against a front face at -8.1, and the cylinder touches the hull only at x<-6.08. With starship-08 the x=0 nozzle would also gap (-8.1 vs -7.945), so the nacelle part of the fix is right and needed. No fix touches THEME_LAYOUTS, doors, slots, the elevator, obstaclesOf or corridorWaypoints, so test/browser-names.test.mjs (lines 137-200) needs no update. Re-run analyze_themes.py after the fixes to confirm noSupport/overhang/hidden/ringClearance/invisibleObstacle(part-*) clear for starship.

Fix ordering and dependencies:
- starship-08 (bake the OCT) must ship with starship-07 (nacelles). Otherwise the north edge moves to z -7.95 and the x=0 nozzle detaches.
- starship-01 (gangways) should land before starship-02 (pockets) and starship-05 (rail x0 = -11.2), because both sit on the gangway deck.

Verification artefacts are in scratchpad/captures/starship/: audit_fix_* are the combined in-page fixes; audit_seam_* are the seam probes.

Tooling caveats:
- scratchpad/shot.py's patch path fails with CSP 'unsafe-eval' because it calls eval(src). Use scratchpad/shot_ss.py, which inlines the patch into the evaluate expression, patches every floor and settles the camera with 3x700 ms re-aims.
- The demo spawns 1-3 floors over time. Patches must hit all floors.
- The visible floor is not always floors[focusIndex]. For that reason the open-door state with pockets could not be re-captured; coverage is computed (doors travel to |z| 1.665, pockets reach 1.9).
- The seam artefact (starship-09) is depth/raster precision in swiftshader. Confirm on a real GPU before spending effort beyond the one-line polygonOffset.
- Patches used: scratchpad/patches/starship/fix_all.js, fix_doors_nozzles.js, rug_poly.js, rug_up.js, noshadow_decks.js, hide_oct.js.

Not filed as a defect (cross-theme design choice): the desk-room screens face +x toward the camera, while the desk slot [8.3,5,E] faces the same way, so seated agents look at the screen backs. starship-06's back panel makes this read correctly.

improvements.sketch: Hoop stand: two posts box(tm.fenceWood, 0.06, 0.95, 0.06) at x +-0.64, z 0.25 from y 0.19, plus a base bar box 1.4x0.06x0.12; all inside corridor-center. Perimeter: 2-3 ICOSA bush clumps (tm.pine, r 0.4-0.5, flatShading) on each outer lobe tip, e.g. (+-12.6, +-7.4) and (+-13.0, +-4.6), where no slot or route goes. Optionally continue the north picket fence around the north lobe rims.

merged.notes:
TOOLING: shot.py with a patch.js fails on this page because the CSP blocks 'unsafe-eval' (EvalError on eval(src)). Use my copy with bypass_csp=True: $AUDIT_OUT/shot_dogs.py (same CLI). In-page reference implementations: $AUDIT_OUT/dogs_patch_fix.js covers dogs-01..07 and 09 together; it used 0.03-thick decals and did not widen the frame, while the numbers in the findings are the final ones. Also dogs_patch_gate.js (dogs-08), dogs_patch_seam.js (dogs-10) and dogs_patch_shadow.js (negative test). Evidence renders are in .../scratchpad/captures/dogs/: audit_fix_iso_se.png, audit_fix_entrance.png and audit_fix_exterior_n.png (batch 1, framed like the originals), audit_orig_entrance_open.png, audit_gatefix_entrance_open.png and audit_seamfix_room_desk.png (batch 2, camera target drifted, so treat as loose confirmation), audit_shadow_compare.png, and crops/audit_*.png. The audit_entrance_open*.png files in that folder (19:00) are not mine.

NOT DEFECTS (analyzer noise): the dev-desks invisibleObstacle covers the thin agility hurdles, which agents should not cross. The wall-* boxes have no walls in the park; after dogs-03 the north fence coincides with wall-north. The elevator frame/door walkThrough hits are the entrance itself. Trunk/foliage and boardFrame frame/trim intersects are intended. Lawn and rug tops at 0.04-0.05 cause the same negligible sink as studio.

ORDERING: do dogs-01 and dogs-08 together (apron depth 3.9 matches frame depth 3.7 and frame x -11.9). Do dogs-03 (bar z +-7.8) before dogs-06 (divider length 5.6 assumes it). dogs-05 and dogs-06 interact: with the flush rim, the z=+-2 picket runs clear the rim, whose ellipse is <=1.91 at |x|>=0.95. Apply dogs-07 after any hydrant-cap improvement.

CONTRACT: no change to THEME_LAYOUTS slots, doors or elevator, or to corridorWaypoints. The only optional obstaclesOf change is dogs-11 (dogs-only box, not pinned by test/browser-names.test.mjs:172-191).

TEST STRATEGY: node tests cannot import three.js builders. Run node --test test/*.test.mjs for the layout contract, then re-run analyze_themes.py for dogs. Expect noSupport, floating, overhang, hidden and ringClearance to clear and invisibleObstacle to drop to wall-*/dev-desks/corridor-center. Then re-shoot iso_se/entrance/exterior_n/center with shot_dogs.py, including one shot after floor.openElevator().

CROSS-THEME: scrollScreen (dogs-04) also affects palace, hanok, starship and cats. buildElevatorDoors door travel (dogs-08) also affects cats and starship. Cats likely shares dogs-06 (no z=+-2 partitions, no lounge prop) by code reading. The centre-feature height pattern (dogs-05) also appears in the starship (h 0.14) and cats (h 0.12) centres.

The polygon test against the real 16-gon rose-gold slab finds more: research tables 25/25 off, desk table 10/25, desk screen at z=5.65 15/25, bell 25/25, research/desk rugs 9/25. findings.location: theme-grounds.js:366-367 (cat-face slab cyl 12.2x8.2 / 11.9x7.9, 16 segments, centred z=0.4); theme-props.js:395-398 (research lowTable + scrollScreen at x=-11.0/-11.2, z=3.6/6.4), :401-403 (desk lowTable 9.5,5 + screens), :404-407 (bell cyl at 10.7,5); theme-grounds.js:376 (rugs rx3 rz2.2 at (±8,±5)); slots theme-layouts.js:140

findings.contractRisk: none. Slots, doors and obstacles stay as they are; only the floor grows under them. The desk-main obstacle (9.0..11.4 x 3.4..6.6) keeps covering the old bell spot. Fill it with the treat jar from the improvements, or accept a small empty collision strip east of the desk.
findings.verifyNote: The defect is real and shows at the default camera. In iso_se.png the far-left research table and the gold bell drum hang over the void. room_research.png shows both west tables off the slab, and room_desk.png / room_lounge_e.png show the bell and the yellow rug overhanging the rim. By maths, slot (-8,6.6) gives (8/11.9)^2+(6.2/7.9)^2 = 1.07, which is outside even the true cream ellipse before the 16-gon loss, and (-10,6.4) is further out. The fix numbers check out: the research tabletop corner (-11.4,7.1) falls inside the 32-gon cream paw (rx3.3/rz3.1 at -9,5), but with only about 0.01 m of margin. Caveats: (1) The renders cited as proof (audit_fix_iso_se/nw) were made by patch_fix.js with a different paw: x +-9.3, 3.2x2.9, cream top 0.04 coplanar with the face, same material. They are not the 9.0 / 3.3x3.1 / 0.045 tinted pad in the text. (2) I rendered the text's variant (verify_cats/patch_final_proposal.js -> captures/cats/audit_verify_final_iso_se.png). The tinted 0.045 pad draws its whole circle over the research and desk room floors, with a visible arc inside each room. So the layering needs the same treatment as cats-02.
findings.fixCorrection: Keep the paw idea and the bell move, with three changes. (a) Do not stack a tinted 0.045 cream disc over the 0.04 face floor. Build the paw lobes into the single merged cat-floor outline described in cats-02. As a fallback, give the paw cream the same velvetCream, put its top BELOW the face top, set castShadow=false, and render-check iso_se for seams. (b) Use cream rx 3.35 / rz 3.15 (rose-gold 3.65 / 3.45) so the research table corner (-11.4,7.1) has a real margin. (c) The bell: base cyl r0.2 h0.06 at (9.5,0.70,5) plus a dome, as proposed.

findings.title: Cat-ear sunrooms are built from CONE4 pyramids: the floor is a sloped skin over a sloped rose-gold pyramid, and the ears are too small for the props on them
findings.evidence: TEST_shot.png (1070-1140,620-800) and iso_se.png (855-895,195-295) show a dark brown wedge in the notch between the ear and the face slab, right of the x=-5.8 cat tree. audit_ear_notch_nw.png (700-940,380-550) shows the ear edge as a sloped brown face meeting the vertical face-slab side. low_s.png (1440-1520,470-520) shows a thin cream plate hovering over a sloped brown underside. The polygon test finds props over the ear/face notch: server tower x=5.6 (6/25 off the slab), archive cat-tree platforms x=-5.8 (5/25) and x=-10.2 (3/25), and the archive/server rug outer edges. The pink inner-ear pyramid apex (y 0.05) touches the rug top (y 0.05).
findings.location: theme-grounds.js:369-371 (cyl(..., CONE4, sx*0.12) for roseGold 4.4/0.44, velvetCream 4.1/0.04, plushPink 2.5/0.03); CONE4 defined at theme-grounds.js:10; rugs :376
findings.rootCause: ConeGeometry has an apex, so a 0.44-tall CONE4 'slab' is a pyramid. Its apex is at y=0 and its rim at y=-0.44. The 0.04 cream 'floor' is another pyramid floating up to 0.41 above that slope near the rim. This is not the CONFIRMED #1 shear class, because the XZ scale is uniform here. Separately, the diamonds (r 4.1 cream, centred ±8,-5.6) leave V-notches against the ellipse right where the server towers and archive trees stand.
findings.fix: Add const DIAMOND = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(1, 1, 1, 4) (a flat 4-sided prism with the same vertex orientation as CONE4) and use it for the three ear layers. Rose-gold: cyl(g, tm.roseGold, 4.8, 4.8, 0.44, sx*7.8, -0.44, -5.8, DIAMOND, sx*0.12). Cream: cyl(g, earCream, 4.5, 4.5, 0.045, sx*7.8, 0, -5.8, DIAMOND, sx*0.12). Pink: cyl(g, tm.plushPink, 2.6, 2.6, 0.004, sx*7.8, 0.045, -6.3, DIAMOND, sx*0.12). The ear tip moves from z≈-10.0 to ≈-10.6 and the side vertex from x≈12.4 to ≈12.6. Do not put the ear cream top at the same 0.04 as the face floor (:367): in-page that gave a dotted z-fight seam along the hidden ear edge (audit_fix_seam_before.png), and 0.035 still leaves a faint line (audit_fix2_seam_after.png). Use 0.045 with a slightly different tint (e.g. 0xf9e4dc 'sunroom cream'), so the diamond edge reads as an intended threshold. Lift the rugs at :376 from y 0.02 to y 0.03 (top 0.06) so they stay above the pink layer (top 0.049). Optionally shrink the top-room rugs to rx 2.8 so their outer edge stays off the rim. Checked with footprint.py mode 'pawA': server tower x=5.6 and all archive trees are on cream, and nothing is off the slab outline. Rendered in audit_fix_iso_se.png and audit_fix_iso_nw.png.
findings.contractRisk: none (floor-only; server slots (5.6..10.2,-5.7) and archive slots stay on the ear)
findings.verifyNote: The geometry claim is correct. cyl(..., CONE4) is scaled (4.4,0.44,4.4), so the 'slab' is a pyramid with its apex at y 0 and its base at -0.44. The cream (0..0.04) is another flat pyramid whose rim floats about 0.41 above the rose-gold slope. low_s.png (zoom: verify_cats/low_s_ear.png) shows the plate over a dark sloped recess. The analyzer reports server tower x=10.2 with one corner 0.41 over the slope. room_server.png (840-875,700-760) shows the purple rug overhanging the face/ear V-notch by about 0.24 m. The 'dark wedge' in iso_se is minor and reads as a slab edge. The XZ scale is uniform, so this is not the shear class in CONFIRMED #1, which the audit also says. But the proposed fix is harmful. DIAMOND r4.5 at (7.8,-5.8), rotY 0.12, has vertices at (8.34,-1.33) and (3.33,-5.26), so the ear reaches into the corridor past z=-2 and across the x=4 divider into dev. With the cream top at 0.045 and a tint, the whole diamond renders over the face floor. I verified this in captures/cats/audit_verify_final_iso_se.png and audit_verify_final_top_ne.png, where the tinted diamond crosses the corridor. The variants that keep the ear below the face also leave seams in this renderer: coplanar 0.04 gives dotted lines (audit_fix_iso_se, audit_fix_seam_before), 0.035 a faint line (audit_fix2_seam_after), 0.035 with shadows off still a faint line (audit_fix4), and my 0.02-below test with shadows off (captures/cats/audit_verify_below_iso_se.png; contrast crop verify_cats/cmp_audit_verify_below_iso_se.png) shows dotted double lines in the east corridor. The original iso_se.png has no line at the same pixels (verify_cats/cmp_iso_se.png).
findings.fixCorrection: Replace the five overlapping floor primitives (face cyl x2, ear cone x2 per side) with ONE cat outline that is the union of the face ellipse, two ear triangles and two paw lobes. Precompute it offline (for example a shapely union of the shapes footprint.py uses in mode pawA, simplified to about 80 points) and hard-code it as CAT_OUTLINE, plus a 0.3-padded CAT_RIM. Rose-gold: new THREE.ExtrudeGeometry(shapeOf(CAT_RIM), {depth:0.44, bevelEnabled:false}).rotateX(Math.PI/2), where shape y = world z and the slab spans y -0.44..0. Cream: ExtrudeGeometry(shapeOf(CAT_OUTLINE), {depth:0.04, bevelEnabled:false}).rotateX(Math.PI/2).translate(0,0.04,0). Keep the pink inner ear as a thin decal (top <=0.044) wholly inside the ear, so its room-side part sits under the rug. Lift the rug tops to 0.06. Size the ears so server tower x=5.6/10.2 and the archive trees are inside, and leave the V-notch filled enough that the server and archive rugs no longer overhang. This one change removes the pyramid slope, the notch overhangs, the seams and the 16-gon facets (cats-08), and gives footprint checks a single polygon. If merging is deferred, do not add any floor layer that overlaps the face floor. At most, swap the rose-gold CONE4 for a flat DIAMOND with its top at -0.01, and re-render iso_se to confirm there are no seams.

findings.title: Invisible corridor walls: obstaclesOf has partitions at z=±2 and full-length x=±4 dividers, but cats builds no z=±2 partition and stops the dividers 0.9 short
findings.evidence: Analyzer invisibleObstacle: part-n-1..4 and part-s-1..4 all have visibleCoverage 0. room_lounge_e.png, iso_se.png and center.png show an open floor between the lounge and the rooms, so agents detour around and bump into nothing to reach the door gaps at x=d.x±0.95. The div-top/bot obstacles span z -8..-2 / 2..8, but the visible rose-gold dividers span only z ±(2.9..7.1). The sisal posts at z=±3.2 sit inside the divider z-range and pierce the 0.1 wall (analyzer intersect x4). The north divider ends at z=-7.1 pass the cream edge (-6.97 at x=4.05) and stand on the rose-gold rim.
findings.location: theme-grounds.js:378-384 (posts cyl at z=±3.2, dividers box 0.1x0.85x4.2 at z=±5); missing z=±2 partitions in buildCatsGround; obstacles theme-layouts.js:168-181
findings.rootCause: buildCatsGround never calls buildStandardPartitions or any equivalent, yet obstaclesOf always emits the part-n/part-s corridor walls and full-length div-* boxes.
findings.fix: In buildCatsGround, build low 'velvet rail' partitions that match the obstacle segments exactly. North (z=-2): x∈[-11.3,-8.95], [-7.05,-0.95], [0.95,7.05], [8.95,11.3]. South (z=+2): x∈[-11.5,-8.95], [-7.05,-0.95], [0.95,7.05], [8.95,11.5]. These are the obstaclesOf segments (door gaps d.x±0.95) clipped to the floor edge, which is |x|≈11.34 at z=-2 and 11.65 at z=+2. Better still, derive them from layoutOf('cats').doors (a pure import). Each segment is box(tm.roseGold, len, 0.5, 0.1, cx, 0, z), a cap box(tm.plushPink, len, 0.08, 0.16, cx, 0.5, z), and sisal posts cyl r 0.09, h 0.75 at both ends (the door jambs). Lengthen the dividers to the corridor: north box(tm.roseGold, 0.1, 0.85, 4.9, x, 0, -4.45) (z -6.9..-2.0, clear of the rim), south box(..., 5.3, x, 0, 4.65) (z 2.0..7.3). Move the sisal posts from z=±3.2 to z=±2.0 so they cap the T-junctions. Rendered in audit_fix_iso_se.png, audit_fix_iso_nw.png and audit_fix2_north_screens.png.
findings.contractRisk: none. Geometry is added to match the existing obstacle boxes, and obstaclesOf and the tests are unchanged. Dogs probably has the same invisible part-* walls.
findings.verifyNote: obstaclesOf emits part-n-1..4 and part-s-1..4 for every theme (theme-layouts.js:173-181), and buildCatsGround builds nothing at z=+-2. The analyzer reports visibleCoverage 0 for all eight. iso_se.png, center.png and room_lounge_e.png show open floor, so agents detour to the door gaps around nothing. The dividers are box 0.1x0.85x4.2 at z=+-5, which spans z +-(2.9..7.1), against div-* boxes at 2..8. The posts at z=+-3.2 pierce the dividers (analyzer intersect). Adding visible rails that match the existing boxes changes no slots, doors or tests. Two details to correct: the rail end x (+-11.3 / +-11.5) assumes the 48-gon face, and with today's 16-gon the cream edge at z=-2 is only x=+-11.18. The jamb posts r0.09 centred at d.x+-0.95 also stick 0.09 into the door gap, where an agent on lane +-0.7 with r 0.24 reaches +-0.94, so they would clip.
findings.fixCorrection: Build as proposed, with two changes. First, centre the sisal jamb posts at d.x +- 1.04 (r 0.09) so they sit outside the 1.9-wide gap. Second, clip the rail ends to the actual floor outline: after the cats-02/08 outline lands, or about +-11.15 at z=-2 and +-11.45 at z=+2 with the current 16-gon slab.

findings.title: Elevator: agents spawn inside the solid frame, and the opening doors slide out past the frame into empty air
findings.evidence: Analyzer walkThrough x3: the frame [-11.595..-11.245] x [-1.1..1.1], h 2.5, and both door panels are not covered by any obstacle. ELEVATOR {x:-11.4, z:0} (theme-layouts.js:133 -> rooms.js:242) lies inside the frame's x-range, so agents spawn (agent.js:57) and leave (agent.js:142,251) inside the block. floor.js:196-199 opens the doors to z centre ±1.24, which puts the panel edges at ±1.665. That is 0.57 beyond the 2.2-wide frame, and cats has no west wall, so open panels hang in the air. entrance.png and room_lounge_w.png show the free-standing frame with nothing beside it.
findings.location: theme-grounds.js:395 (buildElevatorDoors(g, tm.roseGold, tm.plushPink, -11.42, 0)); helper theme-grounds.js:398-403; door travel floor.js:196-199

A spawned agent (x -11.4, r 0.24, so edge -11.64) stands in front of the doors. At z=±1.1 the 48-gon slab reaches x≈-11.99, so the frame rests on the rose-gold rim. Residual: the wings sit partly outside wall-west-n/s (those boxes stop at x=-11.88). Agents approach the elevator on lanes |z|≤0.7 (LANES 15 x LANE_GAP 0.1), so they never reach |z|≥1.1; accept this. findings.contractRisk: none for cats. ELEVATOR and the lounge door stay at x=-11.4, so the slots and tests are unchanged. If buildElevatorDoors itself is widened, check studio/office/palace/hanok/starship/dogs (starship and dogs elevators already float off their footprints, CONFIRMED #3).
findings.verifyNote: The frame box 0.35x2.5x2.2 at x=-11.42 spans -11.595..-11.245, so ELEVATOR (-11.4,0) (theme-layouts.js:131, applied at rooms.js:242) spawns and despawns agents inside it (agent.js:57/142/251; safeSpawnPos ignores the frame because it is not an obstacle). floor.js:196-199 opens the doors to o=1.24, which puts the panel edges at +-1.665, beyond the +-1.1 frame. audit_entrance_open.png shows both panels hanging in the air. (2) The closed doors span x -11.66..-11.58, so a spawned agent's back edge (-11.64) overlaps them by about 0.06. That is minor.
findings.fixCorrection: As proposed, ordered after the slab change (CYL48 or the merged outline must reach x<=-11.98 at z=+-1.1). Optionally use x=-11.85 so the closed doors clear a spawned agent completely, but then extend the rim/outline to x=-12.03 at z=+-1.1.

findings.title: Centre cat tower: base disc and platforms reach into the ring walk lanes (feet sink 0.12, heads hit the pads)
findings.evidence: Analyzer ringClearance x4. The base cyl r 2.1, h 0.12 spans z ±2.1 over the walk ring (z = ±1.4 + lane*0.25, so |z| ∈ [1.225,1.575]). It also pokes 0.1 past z=±2 into the dev and meeting doorways. The pads (r 0.78) at y 1.02-2.02 reach z -1.23..1.33. In center.png the orange cat walks on the rim of the 0.12-high disc. Biped cat agents carry their collar at y≈1.1 (pet-mesh.js:80), so their heads at ~1.5-1.7 pass through the 1.02-1.57 pads on the north lane.

findings.rootCause: three.js composes T*R*S. scale(w*0.74, h, d*0.74) is applied to the 4-cone's diamond (vertices on the axes) before rotation.y=PI/4, so the result is a rotated rhombus, not an axis-aligned rectangle-based pyramid. The intent was rotate first, then scale (S*R).
findings.fix: In theme-grounds.js add `const ROOF4 = new THREE.ConeGeometry(1, 1, 4).rotateY(Math.PI / 4);`. Do NOT rotate CONE4: buildCatsGround :369-371 uses it for the ear slabs. In roofEave use `new THREE.Mesh(ROOF4, mat)`, keep scale (w*0.74, h, d*0.74), which gives a footprint of 1.046*w (about 2% overhang, as in the verified experiment), and delete line 68. This fixes all 7 call sites. In the same change, pull the palace north eaves back to the colonnade line so they stop covering north-room furniture: :188 -> roofEave(g, tm.tile, tm.dancheong, 9.2, 0.95, 1.3, 0, 2.45, -8.15); :189 and :190 -> roofEave(g, tm.tile, tm.dancheong, 8.2, 0.72, 1.0, -/+8, 2.3, -7.95). The trim boxes then span z -8.75..-7.55 and still cap the pillars at z=-7.8. Hanok :234 already sits on the wall line, and the gates need no size change. The remaining wall and roof occlusion from north cameras is handled by xcut-10 and the facade-cutaway improvement.
findings.contractRisk: CONE4 is shared with the cats ears and must stay unrotated. Roofs are not in obstaclesOf, so collision and layouts are unaffected. The node smoke test (test/page-approval-office.test.mjs:342-343) only checks that 2 door leaves are returned. After the fix, the palace and hanok lounge sign anchors sit inside the gate pyramids (xcut-14). Roof tops (max y 3.56) stay below the next floor's slab bottom (about 4.5 with FLOOR_GAP 5.4).
