findings.fix: Add `const OCT8 = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(1, 1, 1, 8).rotateY(Math.PI / 8);` and call cyl(g, tm.hull, 11.2, 8.6, 0.52, 0, -0.52, 0, OCT8) and cyl(g, tm.hullDeck, 10.7, 8.2, 0.03, 0, 0, 0, OCT8), with no rotY. The result is flat sides at x=±10.35 (|z|<=3.29) and z=±7.95 (|x|<=4.29). Guard the helper: in cyl(), `if (rotY % (Math.PI / 2) !== 0 && rx !== rz) console.warn('cyl: bake rotation into geometry when rx != rz')`. The node harness assertion (improvements) makes this a test failure.
findings.contractRisk: The hull's west edge moves from -9.9 to -10.35, so the xcut-02 gangway length depends on this change. The east flat at 10.35 still leaves the starship lounge bench (x 9.1..11.1) off the hull (xcut-09). The HEX wing pods (rotY 0) are unaffected.
findings.verifyNote: Recomputed the vertices: the scaled unit octagon (11.2, 0) rotated 22.5 degrees gives (10.35, -4.29), and (7.92, 6.08) gives (9.65, 2.59). That is the audit's skewed outline, and its west edge at z=0 is about -9.9. starship/top.png vs audit_rooffix_top.png shows the asymmetric and then the symmetric hull. OCT8 = CylinderGeometry(1,1,1,8).rotateY(PI/8) gives flats at x=+-10.35 (|z|<=3.29) and z=+-7.95 (|x|<=4.29). The deck flats are +-9.89 and +-7.58, which leaves a sensible rim. The warn guard is harmless for the HEX pods (rotY 0) and the cats ears (rx==rz). The Proxy stub tolerates the module-level .rotateY call. P2 on its own, but xcut-02 and xcut-09 depend on it, so land it before them.

findings.title: Floor.update slides every theme's door leaves to z=±1.24: they overshoot the 2.2-wide portal frame and push into the palace and hanok gate posts
findings.evidence: door_open_patch.js (elevT=1e6) measured leaf centres at z=±1.16..1.24 with width 0.85, so the outer edge reaches ±1.665. That is past the frame half-depth of 1.1 (buildElevatorDoors) and past the gate-post inner faces at 1.03 (palace posts z±1.25, r 0.22) and 1.0 (hanok z±1.2, r 0.2). Screenshots: $AUDIT_OUT/captures/cats/audit_entrance_open.png and captures/starship/audit_entrance_open.png (leaves hanging past the portal in mid-air), captures/dogs/audit_entrance_open_sw.png, captures/hanok/audit_entrance_open.png and captures/palace/audit_entrance_open.png (leaves pushed into the posts), captures/studio/audit_entrance_open_sw.png (leaves slide over the wall face). An open portal also shows the same solid frame face, with no shaft depth.
findings.location: public/js/floor.js:195-199 (o = 0.46 + doorOpen*0.78 for every theme); public/js/theme-grounds.js:398-403, 208-211, 259-262; triggered by agent.js:64 openElevator() on each spawn
findings.rootCause: One hard-coded slide distance is used for every portal and gate, whatever their frame or post spacing.
findings.fix: Use telescoping leaves pinned at the closed outer edge 0.885, which is inside every frame and post. In Floor.update: `const inner = 0.035 + this.doorOpen * 0.73; for (const [i, s] of [[0, -1], [1, 1]]) { const d = this.doors[i]; d.scale.z = 0.885 - inner; d.position.z = s * (inner + d.scale.z / 2); }`. Fully open, the gap is 1.53 (an agent is 0.48 wide) and no leaf passes |z|=0.885. In buildElevatorDoors add a dark recess so an open portal shows depth: box(g, mats().dark, 0.02, 2.1, 1.77, x + 0.176, 0, z, false). Optional for the palace and hanok wooden gates: hinge-swing leaves (leaf inside a pivot Group at z=±0.885, pivot.rotation.y = ±doorOpen*1.3, selected via leaf.userData.swing).
findings.contractRisk: buildThemeGround must still return an array of exactly 2 leaves (test/page-approval-office.test.mjs:342-343); carry any mode flag on leaf.userData or as an array property. The leaves' initial scale.z (0.84/0.85) is now driven by update. floor.js is the only consumer of this.doors (grep).
findings.verifyNote: floor.js:197-199 opens the leaves to +-1.24, so a 0.85-deep leaf reaches +-1.665 against the 1.1 frame half-depth and the 1.03/1.0 inner faces of the gate posts. cats/audit_entrance_open.png and starship/audit_entrance_open.png show leaves hanging past the frame. studio/iso_se.png and office/iso_se.png caught the doors open at the default camera with the leaves past the frame ends. The telescoping formula reproduces today's closed state exactly (inner 0.035, scale 0.85, z +-0.46). Fully open it gives leaves at 0.765..0.885 and a 1.53 gap, inside every frame and post. floor.js is the only consumer, and the test only counts 2 leaves.
findings.fixCorrection: Same formula. Give the recess box height 2.08, not 2.1, so its top face is not coplanar with the leaf tops at y=2.1 where they overlap. The leaves will look like they shrink rather than slide. The palace and hanok hinge swing is the nicer look for wooden gates.

findings.title: The shared corridor partitions (part-n-*/part-s-*), div tails and lounge-sofa collision boxes have no visible geometry in open themes, so agents follow invisible doorways
findings.evidence: analysis/REPORT.txt invisibleObstacle: all 8 part-* boxes have coverage 0-0.005 in hanok, starship, dogs and cats. lounge-sofa is 0 in dogs and cats. The x=±4 dividers are drawn shorter than the 6.0-long div-* boxes (dogs 4.4, cats 4.2, starship 5.2, hanok 5.4), leaving invisible 0.3-0.8 tails at z -2.8..-2 and 2..2.8. Palace's hand-coded partition gaps are 2.2 wide vs 1.9 in collision. Screenshots: $AUDIT_OUT/captures/dogs/iso_se.png and captures/hanok/iso_se.png show open lawn and courtyard, yet route() (placement.js:258-282) always sends agents through the door points at x=-8/0/8.
findings.location: public/js/theme-layouts.js:167-181 (shared div/part boxes), :203 (lounge-sofa), :205-216 (existing per-theme gating); public/js/theme-grounds.js:141-159 (buildStandardPartitions, studio/office only), :196-201 (palace, hand-coded), :240-245, :295-300, :341-344, :379-384 (x=±4 only)
findings.rootCause: obstaclesOf is one shared contract, but each builder draws (or omits) the matching walls by hand, so collision and visuals drift apart.
findings.sharedHelper: buildCorridorRails(g, theme, style) derived from obstaclesOf
findings.fix: Strategy (one choice): keep the shared collision contract and draw it. Add buildCorridorRails(g, theme, style) to theme-grounds. It iterates obstaclesOf(theme).filter((o) => /^(part|div)-/.test(o.tag)) and draws each box over x0..x1 and z0..z1 with style {mat, capMat, h, capH, shadow}. Gaps then follow layout.doors automatically (for example, the hanok research door at -8.4 ends part-s-1 at -9.35). Keep heights <= 0.5 so agents (1.7 tall) stay visible: hanok, a 0.35 dark-wood rail on a 0.06 granite kerb; starship, a 0.25 hullTrim kerb plus a 0.5 forceField strip (no shadow); dogs, a 0.45 lawnDark low hedge (flatShading) or a 0.5 picket fence; cats, 0.4 roseGold posts every 1.0 with a plushPink rope. Palace, studio and office can migrate later (they already match within 0.15). For lounge-sofa, add the shared lounge bench to dogs and cats (the same lowTable(..., 10.1, 1.58, 2.0, 0.55, 0.42) that palace, hanok and starship use), or gate the box per theme the way lounge-water is gated.
findings.contractRisk: Existing tests are unaffected: obstacle counts, slot and route checks in browser-names.test.mjs:353-370 do not change. Rejected alternative: a theme-aware obstaclesOf without part-* boxes. route() and doorOf would still force door waypoints, so agents would keep turning at invisible doorways, and obs.length would drop to 21 against the `>= 20` assertion at browser-names.test.mjs:356. Partition visuals must not exceed 0.5 in height, or they occlude agents from the default camera.
findings.verifyNote: The coverage data is right: part-* boxes are 0 in hanok, starship, dogs and cats, and lounge-sofa is 0 in dogs and cats. The div tails are real (dogs fence 4.4, cats 4.2, starship 5.2, hanok 5.4 against 6.0 boxes). The proposed buildCorridorRails, however, filters /^(part|div)-/. That would redraw the x=+-4 dividers on top of the existing fences, hanji and force fields every theme already has, giving doubled walls and stacked transparent planes in starship. The contractRisk arithmetic is off: dropping the 8 part-* boxes leaves 21 (ring) or 23 (dogs and cats), which still passes >= 20. The rejection still stands on the route()/doorOf argument.
findings.fixCorrection: Draw only the part-* boxes from obstaclesOf (filter /^part-/). Fix the div tails by stretching each theme's existing x=+-4 divider meshes to the full z span of their div box: -8..-2 and 2..8, or -7.85..-2.12 where a north fence or wall sits. Keep rails at or below 0.5 high and give transparent strips shadow=false. Add the lounge bench to dogs and cats, or gate lounge-sofa per theme.

findings.evidence: analysis raisedFloor: 29 slots per theme, with tops 0.11 in palace and 0.14/0.17 in hanok. In $AUDIT_OUT/captures/hanok/room_archive.png the agent's feet sink into the maru.
findings.location: public/js/theme-grounds.js:177-182 (palace wood h 0.08 + rug at 0.09), :225-231 (hanok wood h 0.14 + rug at 0.15). Props seated on those floors: theme-grounds.js:241 and :243 (hanji at 0.14, caps 1.22); theme-props.js:52 (populateShelves y 0.08), :93-94, :108, :135-141 (palace 0.08), :166-167, :172, :180, :207-210 (hanok 0.14)

findings.title: The scrollScreen helper is a single-sided plane with no back, so screens vanish from north and west cameras and leave two floating bars
findings.evidence: $AUDIT_OUT/captures/dogs/audit_room_desk_from_w.png: the desk screens disappear and only the blue and yellow bars float. The helper is used about 32 times across the 5 prop builders, and the research and desk screens face +x, so any west-side camera sees their backs. furniture.js monitor() has a dark backing box and does not have this problem.
findings.location: public/js/theme-props.js:21-32 (scrollScreen); all callers in buildPalaceProps, buildHanokProps, buildStarshipProps, buildDogsProps and buildCatsProps
findings.rootCause: PlaneGeometry with the default FrontSide material and no backing mesh.
findings.fix: Add a back panel inside scrollScreen: `box(grp, frameMat, w + 0.04, h + 0.06, 0.03, 0, 0.06, -0.02);`. The plane at z=+0.02 stays in front, and from behind it reads as a scroll or board. Do NOT set side=DoubleSide on M.screens.*, because those materials are shared with furniture.js monitor().
findings.contractRisk: Adds about 32 meshes that reuse the shared BOX geometry, so no new allocations.
findings.verifyNote: dogs/audit_room_desk_from_w.png shows only blue and yellow bars where the screens should be. cats/iso_nw.png and exterior_n.png show the same on every desk seen from behind. The backing box spans y 0.06..h+0.12 and z -0.035..-0.005, behind the plane at z +0.02, and reuses BOX, so no new geometry. Not using DoubleSide is right, because it would show mirrored text. There are about 41 call sites, not 32, which does not matter.

findings.location: public/js/theme-grounds.js:114-116 (studio north/west wall), :135-136 (office), :233-234 (hanok), :188-190 (palace eaves), :209 and :260 (gates seen from the west); public/js/scene.js:64-68
findings.rootCause: The diorama is authored for the SE camera only, with no view-dependent cutaway.
findings.fix: Short term: the palace eave shrink in xcut-01. Proper fix: tag facade meshes (userData.facade = [nx, nz]: north walls and eaves (0,-1), west walls and gates (-1,0)). Each frame, hide or ghost them when dot(cameraDirXZ, n) > 0.25, with 0.05 hysteresis. The default SE camera has dot -0.707 and is unaffected. See improvement 'Camera-facing facade cutaway'.

findings.verifyNote: OrbitControls sets no azimuth limit (scene.js:64-68). The 2.2-2.8 north walls and the eaves hide the north rooms from NE and NW, which is the normal diorama trade-off, so P2. Cutaway by dot(cameraDirXZ, n) does not change the default SE view. A cheaper interim fix is to limit azimuth.

findings.title: Rebuild leak: furniture.js allocates 10 geometries per studio/office build, and nothing is ever disposed on theme switch or floor prune
findings.evidence: $AUDIT_OUT/xcut/leak_probe.py measured renderer.info.memory.geometries on 1 floor: 29 at start, then 61, 82 and 103 after each of three 7-theme rebuild cycles (+21 per cycle at steady state), and 113 after one more studio rebuild (+10). A studio archGroup has 275 meshes but only 16 unique geometries. Each studio/office rebuild adds about 2.5k vertices (roughly 80-100 KB of VBOs plus VAOs and JS objects) per floor. With the 10-floor #bench, one switch to studio leaks 100 geometries. The InstancedMesh book shelves (instanceMatrix/instanceColor) are not counted in info.memory and are never disposed either. Floor.dispose, called from office.js:345 pruneEmptyFloors, frees nothing. screenMat canvases are created only once, because mats() is cached.
findings.location: public/js/furniture.js:169, 175, 177-179 (plus LineBasicMaterial per call), 188, 190, 226, 231, 234, 237, 251; :127 and theme-props.js:63 (InstancedMesh); public/js/floor.js:65 (archGroup.clear), :202-205 (dispose)
findings.rootCause: furniture.js predates the module-level-geometry pattern that agent-mesh.js:8-19, theme-props.js:9-12 and theme-grounds.js:7-12 use. archGroup.clear() only detaches meshes.
findings.fix: Hoist the 10 geometries to module constants: RESEARCH_PED = CylinderGeometry(0.2, 0.3, 0.95, 12); GLOBE_BALL = IcosahedronGeometry(0.8, 2); GLOBE_WIRE = WireframeGeometry(IcosahedronGeometry(0.84, 1)); MAST = CylinderGeometry(0.04, 0.06, 1.8, 8); DISH = SphereGeometry(0.42, 16, 8, 0, 2π, 0, π/2.6); MUG = CylinderGeometry(0.07, 0.07, 0.16, 10); BOOTH_PED = CylinderGeometry(0.4, 0.48, 0.86, 16); BOOTH_RING = TorusGeometry(0.38, 0.026, 8, 24); BOOTH_CORE = IcosahedronGeometry(0.26, 1); BOTTLE = CylinderGeometry(0.17, 0.17, 0.5, 12). Move the LineBasicMaterial into mats() as M.wire. In Floor.rebuildTheme, before clear(): `this.archGroup.traverse((o) => { if (o.isInstancedMesh) o.dispose(); });`. InstancedMesh.dispose frees only the instance buffers, never the shared BOX or materials. Do the same in Floor.dispose and also dispose the Board texture. Never dispose module-level geometries (scene BOX; furniture PLANE/POT/LEAF/LEAF_S; theme-props PLANE/CYL/TORUS/ICOSA; theme-grounds CYL/HEX/OCT/CONE4/TORUS/ICOSA) or the cached mats()/themeMats()/M.screens/board.material.
findings.contractRisk: A node test with the Proxy stub (page-approval-office.test.mjs:14-31) constructs geometries at module load, which is fine. Accidentally disposing a shared geometry blanks every floor, so restrict dispose to InstancedMesh.
findings.verifyNote: furniture.js allocates exactly 10 geometries per studio/office build: research 5, desk 4, lounge 1. It also creates a LineBasicMaterial per call. archGroup.clear() never disposes anything. In r160, InstancedMesh.dispose() releases the instance buffers through the renderer's dispose listener, and restricting dispose to InstancedMesh avoids blanking shared geometry. A theme switch is rare, so P2.

findings.title: Procedural layouts use Math.random: bookshelves differ per floor and per rebuild, so captures cannot be reproduced
findings.evidence: theme-props.js:56-58 (populateShelves, palace and hanok) and furniture.js:120-122 (buildArchive, studio and office) draw book widths, heights and colours from Math.random on every build. furniture.js:58-62 screenMat is random once per page. Successive captures of the same theme differ, which blocks screenshot diffs and any golden-image check.
findings.location: public/js/theme-props.js:49-73; public/js/furniture.js:112-140, :44-73

improvements.title: Recording three.js stub harness: build every theme in node CI and assert geometry invariants
improvements.rationale: CI (.github/workflows/test.yml) runs only `node --test test/*.test.mjs` on Node 22/24, with zero dependencies and no browser. A precedent exists: test/page-approval-office.test.mjs:14-31 registers a node:module loader that maps 'three' and 'three/*' to a Proxy stub and already calls buildThemeGround and build*Props (:329-363). Upgrading that stub to a recording one turns most of this audit into CI tests.
improvements.location: new test/fixtures/three-record.mjs (plus the loader extracted from page-approval-office.test.mjs:14-31 into test/fixtures/three-loader.mjs) and new test/theme-geometry.test.mjs
improvements.sketch: The stub implements Object3D (position, scale, rotation set/copy/setScalar, add, children, traverse, userData), Group, Mesh, InstancedMesh, LineSegments, geometry classes that record {type, parameters, bakedRotY via rotateY()} and count constructor calls, materials (color.set/getHex, transparent, opacity), Color, Matrix4 (makeScale().setPosition()), Vector3, CanvasTexture and constants. It also stubs document.createElement('canvas') and getComputedStyle, as :330-334 do. Compute analytic world AABBs and outlines: boxes from scale, cylinders and cones from their n vertices through baked R, S, mesh R and the parent chain. Assertions: (a) no mesh has rotation.y off a multiple of π/2 with scale.x != scale.z and radialSegments in {4,6,8} (fails today: 7 roofEave + 2 OCT); (b) no returned led lies inside another mesh's AABB (fails today: starship 20); (c) every slot, door, spawn and mesh base centre is over a ground mesh (fails today: starship and dogs elevator, cats desk); (d) ground top under slots <= 0.05 (fails today: palace, hanok); (e) in ring themes every centre mesh with top > 0.05 has |z| <= 0.92 (fails today: starship, dogs, cats); (f) each part-*/div-*/lounge-sofa obstacle is at least 60% covered by meshes spanning y 0.25 or more (fails today: hanok, starship, dogs, cats); (g) the door formula at doorOpen=1 keeps leaves within ±0.885 (fails today: all); (h) a second build of each theme constructs 0 geometries (fails today: studio and office, 10 each); (i) Math.random is not called during a build (fails today: populateShelves, buildArchive); (j) every PlaneGeometry screen has a box within 0.05 behind it (fails today: scrollScreen). Run with `npm test`.

improvements.title: Committed dev-only browser audit and capture runner with a per-category baseline

This is documented as a manual pre-merge step and is not in CI.

improvements.title: Seeded RNG module for procedural props
improvements.rationale: Deterministic shelves and screens make captures diffable and let the harness forbid Math.random during builds (xcut-12).
improvements.sketch: `export function mulberry32(seed) { return () => { seed |= 0; seed = (seed + 0x6D2B79F5) | 0; let t = Math.imul(seed ^ (seed >>> 15), 1 | seed); t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t; return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296; }; }` plus seedOf(str). Pass an rng into populateShelves, buildArchive and screenMat. Node test: same seed gives the same first 10 values.

improvements.title: Per-theme style table for the shared structural kit (corridor rails, elevator portal and pad, lounge bench, backed screen)
improvements.rationale: Each theme hand-rolls the same structural pieces, and the pieces drift from the collision and layout data (xcut-02, 04, 05, 08). One kit driven by a style table gives every theme the same structural guarantees while keeping its own look.

Each theme builder calls buildCorridorRails(g, theme, STRUCT[theme].rail), buildElevatorDoors(g, theme, STRUCT[theme].portal) and loungeBench(g, STRUCT[theme].bench, ANCHORS[theme].loungeBench). Studio, office and palace can opt in gradually.

merged.notes:
Contracts the plan must keep:
1. buildThemeGround must return an array of exactly 2 door leaves (test/page-approval-office.test.mjs:342-343; floor.js:198-199).
2. Every build*Props must return non-empty leds and a globe (page-approval-office.test.mjs:360-363). floor.js:189 would also crash on empty leds.
3. obstaclesOf results are cached and frozen. test/browser-names.test.mjs:353-370 requires at least 20 boxes per theme, slots that do not overlap any box, and obstacle-free routes from every door, including the lounge door.
4. browser-names.test.mjs:172-190 pins hanok ELEVATOR.x = -11.6 and the ring detour z >= 1.3.
5. CONE4 is shared with the cats ear slabs. Add ROOF4 and OCT8 constants; never call rotateY on a shared geometry.
6. Never dispose module-level geometries or cached materials.

Test strategy constraints: CI runs only node --test on Node 22/24, with no browser and zero dependencies. The only way to exercise the three.js builders in CI is the node:module loader stub pattern already in page-approval-office.test.mjs:14-31; extend it into a recording stub rather than inventing a new mechanism. Pure invariants on layout data can live next to theme-layouts.js. The page CSP (src/server-guard.mjs:22) blocks eval, so scratch shot.py with a patch.js fails with EvalError. Use $AUDIT_OUT/xcut/multishot.py, which inlines the patch into the evaluated function, and any committed runner must do the same. pages.yml deploys all of public/, so keep audit tooling in scripts/.

Analyzer caveats:
- The AABB-based 'intersect' and slot-clearance checks give false positives for rotated groups. The studio/office research globe wireframe AABB looks 0.19 inside slot research[2], but the sphere actually clears it by about 0.3.
- support_probe's elevator.top=0 values for starship and dogs are the frame's own bottom face, not floor.
- The 'outside' category flags intentional terraces in office and palace.

Theme-specific items seen but left to the theme auditors:
- Starship engine-core LEDs are hidden inside the columns (CONFIRMED #2); harness assertion (b) catches it.
- Starship archive slots are 0.01 from the 0.3-high crystal plinths.
- Dogs archive slot[0] overlaps the pine foliage by 0.03 at head height (pine at -11.2,-6.2), and the pine trunk is not in obstaclesOf.
- The dogs north fence (z=-7.4) sits inside the wall-north box's clearance band.
- The cats research south-west corner (slot[1] at -10,6.4, desk and rug) is off the face 16-gon.
- Dark seam lines between the starship OCT and HEX decks (0.03 vs 0.04 tops).

Suggested implementation order:
1. Pure geometry data and node harness (tests fail first).
2. ROOF4 and OCT8 plus palace eave shrink (P0).
3. Elevator data, pads and spawn offsets (P0).
4. Door telescoping.
5. Corridor rails and lounge bench.
6. Centre-feature shrink.
7. Thin floors.
8. Backed scrollScreen.
9. Leak, RNG, transparency, signs and dead code.
10. Facade cutaway last; it needs the camera passed from Office.update to the floors.

Re-run captures/*/iso_se, iso_ne, iso_nw, entrance and center after each step.

plan.markdown:
# Place Theme Repair Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Repair every verified broken building and object in the seven office-sim place themes (studio, office, palace, hanok, starship, dogs, cats), lock each repair in with node-run geometry invariants, and leave theme-identity polish as optional follow-up tasks.

**Architecture:** First a recording three.js stub lets `node --test` build all seven themes through the real `Floor.prototype.rebuildTheme` dispatch and assert geometry invariants (shear, hidden meshes, floor support, floor height, ring clearance, collision/visual coverage, globe and route clearance, allocation, determinism, coplanar tops, backed screens) against a ratcheting allowlist of today's known failures. Shared root causes are then fixed once in shared helpers and in pure layout data (roof geometry, elevator/gate data and door kinematics, corridor rails derived from `obstaclesOf`, floor heights, centre-feature sizing, scroll screens, globe boxes, rebuild hygiene), followed by per-theme P0/P1 fixes and optional P2 tasks. Every task starts by removing its entries from the allowlist (red) and ends green.

**Tech Stack:** three.js 0.160 (CDN importmap), vanilla ES modules, node --test.

**Spec:** "User request 2026-10-23: improve place themes; fix broken objects and buildings" + audit evidence `$AUDIT_OUT/analysis/REPORT.txt` (captures and per-theme `geometry.json` under `.../scratchpad/captures/<theme>/`; ids such as `studio-01` refer to the verified audit JSON from the planning run; every number a P0-P2 fix needs is inlined below, while Task 27 cites improvement sketches by title, so that JSON must accompany this plan).

---

## Global Constraints

- Zero npm dependencies: tests use only `node:test`, `node:assert`, `node:module`; three.js stays on the CDN importmap.
- English identifiers; comments follow the existing Korean comment style; no emoticons in markdown.
- Files stay at or below about 500 lines. `theme-grounds.js` (403) and `theme-props.js` (409) are split in Task 4 before anything grows; every task's verify step runs `wc -l public/js/theme-*.js public/js/furniture.js public/js/floor.js`.
- The `theme-layouts.js` contract (THEME_LAYOUTS slots/doors/elevator, `obstaclesOf`, `corridorWaypoints`) is stable except where a task says otherwise: Task 6 (elevator data), Task 12 (research-globe boxes), Task 21 (studio/office extra boxes), Task 22 (lounge-sofa table). Every `obstaclesOf` change re-runs `test/browser-names.test.mjs:353-370` (all 7 themes: slots clear at r 0.24, door-to-slot routes clear at r 0.16, at least 20 boxes) and keeps the pins at `:172-190` (hanok `ELEVATOR.x === -11.6`, ring detour `abs(z) >= 1.3`) and `segmentHitsObstacle(-8, 2.9, -8, 6.6, 0.2, 'studio') === true`. Palace obstacles are pinned indirectly by that loop too (palace-m03).
- Low-poly primitives only; no external assets, textures or loaders.
- `npm test` stays green after every task (baseline 1299 passing plus the new tests). Known failures live only in the Task 2 allowlist `test/fixtures/theme-known.mjs`, never as skipped tests.
- Return contracts (test/page-approval-office.test.mjs:338-363): `buildThemeGround` returns exactly 2 door leaves; every `build*Props` returns non-empty `leds` and a `globe`; builders only call `g.add` on the passed parent.
- New geometries and materials are module-level constants or members of the cached `mats()` / `themeMats()`; never created per build (harness check `alloc`). Never call `rotateY` or `dispose` on a shared geometry (`CONE4` also feeds the cats ears until Task 19). Never call `themed()` outside `mats()` (scene.js:19-25 pushes every call into THEMED).
- Floor-layer rule: agent feet are at y = 0 (agent.js/agent-mesh.js); walkable tops are at most 0.06; any new decal or pad top differs by at least 0.005 from every overlapping flat top of a different material (harness `coplanar`).
- Centre-feature rule (ring themes): anything taller than 0.08 stays inside the corridor-center box (`abs(x) <= obstacle.x1 - 0.35`, `abs(z) <= 0.92`); the ring lane body band is `abs(zRing) +/- 0.375` (lane offset 0.7 x 0.25 plus the 0.2 walking radius `resolveObstacleCollision(pos, 0.2, ...)` uses in Agent.update).
- Camera rule: the default camera looks from SE (+x, +z). Opaque corridor rails are at most 0.75 tall, translucent strips at most 1.0 with `castShadow = false`; no prop taller than 0.8 within 0.6 of the east (x > 11) or south (z > 7.3) edge; tall identity props go on north or west walls.
- Collision/visual rule: a visible barrier lies inside the obstacle box it represents, and nothing visible enters a door gap (`d.x +/- 0.95`).
- Line numbers are pre-split (commit 369f29b). After Task 4, locate code by function name plus the quoted literal; Task 4 lists every move.
- Process (user policy): implement in a git worktree under `.worktrees/` cut from `origin/master`; commit only when the user has approved committing; every commit message ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Commit subjects follow the repo style (`test(themes): ...`, `fix(themes): ...`, `refactor(themes): ...`, `feat(themes): ...`).
- Render checks. `SCRATCH=$AUDIT_OUT` (volatile; Task 29 commits a runner). Serve the worktree, not the main checkout: add a `.claude/launch.json` entry (or use the preview tool) running `node bin/office-sim.mjs --port 4319 --replay test/fixtures/replay/7e7e7e7e-1111-4222-8333-444455556666.jsonl --speed 4 --loop`. Shots: `OFFICE_SIM_URL=http://localhost:4319/ python3 -I $SCRATCH/plan/multishot.py <theme> $SCRATCH/captures/<theme>/audit_T<n> <patch.js or -> <view...>`.
